# SchemeDB — NFL Tactical Scheme & All-22 Playbook Visualizer

> SchemeDB is a high-fidelity football analytics and tactical engineering workstation containing 45 scheme systems (25 Offensive, 20 Defensive) spanning modern NFL, historical NFL, and college football, 180 hand-authored plays with Catmull-Rom spline trajectory waypoints, 0.0s–1.2s disguise mesh window telemetry, and 17 coaching lineage trees spanning 53 coaches and patriarchs.

## Overview & Architecture

- **Mathematical Engine**: 22-player waypoint interpolation using Catmull-Rom cubic splines with exact arc-length parameterization for realistic deceleration, plant steps, and break angles.
- **Coordinate System**: Field dimensions are LOS-relative yards where `x` represents cross-field position (`0.0` left sideline to `53.33` right sideline, hashes at `23.36` and `29.97`) and `y` represents depth relative to the Line of Scrimmage (`y < 0` backfield, `y > 0` downfield).
- **Disguise Mesh Window (0.0s – 1.2s)**: The critical pre-snap to early post-snap window where constraint plays mirror primary base runs/passes. Ghost overlays and conflict telemetry quantify defender commitment frames.
- **Play Sequencing Framework**: Every play defines explicit game-plan relationships:
  - `setsUp`: Plays unlocked or amplified by establishing this call.
  - `playsOff`: Complementary plays whose visual picture this call mimics.
  - `tell`: The singular visual cue distinguishing this play from its partner.

- **Direct Scheme Links**: `https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme={scheme-id}` (e.g., `https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone`)

## Offensive Scheme Families (25 Systems / 100 Plays)

### Kyle Shanahan's Wide Zone Family (`shanahan-wide-zone`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Kyle Shanahan (San Francisco 49ers)
- **Philosophy**: The premier modern NFL offensive system built on horizontal stretch sequencing. The base Outside Zone run and its three constraint counters (Play-Action Deep Over, Naked Bootleg, and Jet Motion) present an identical visual picture to the defense for the first ~1.2 seconds, forcing defenders into impossible run-pass conflicts.
- **Plays**:
  - [Outside Zone Left](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=outside-zone) (`outside-zone`): Stretch the defense horizontally from sideline to sideline to create wide running lanes and force linebackers into overpursuit.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Flow LB). Tell cue: Base run action with full offensive line reach-and-seal flow and RB pressing the playside tackle landmark.
  - [Wide Zone Play-Action Deep Over](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=play-action-over) (`play-action-over`): Exploit second-level defenders overplaying the run by throwing deep intermediate passes into the vacated zone behind them.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Flow LB). Tell cue: Backside WR (Z) cuts across the formation behind linebackers on a deep Over route instead of stalking downfield.
  - [Wide Zone Naked Bootleg](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=naked-bootleg) (`naked-bootleg`): Punish aggressive backside defensive ends and pursuit defenders who crash down the line against wide zone runs.. Key conflict: Backside Defensive End (Contain) & Strong Safety. Tell cue: QB pulls the ball out of the mesh and rolls right away from the offensive line flow, while TE releases into the backside flat.
  - [Jet Motion Outside Zone Left](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=jet-motion-oz) (`jet-motion-oz`): Force the defense to shift gap fits and rotate secondary coverage laterally before/at snap, creating perimeter numbers advantages.. Key conflict: Overhang / Strong Safety & Playside Cornerback. Tell cue: Z-receiver runs full-speed jet motion across the formation before/at snap, creating a 2nd mesh point in the backfield.

### Klint Kubiak's Motion & Split-Zone / Leak Family (`kubiak-split-zone`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Klint Kubiak (Las Vegas Raiders)
- **Philosophy**: A masterclass in modern Shanahan-Kubiak sequencing. By marrying heavy 12-personnel condensed formations, pre-snap glide/orbit motion, and under-center split-zone run mechanics, Kubiak presents an identical visual picture before unleashing devastating intermediate Dagger shots, explosive backside Y-Leaks, and rapid perimeter tosses.
- **Plays**:
  - [Split Zone (Slice)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=split-zone-slice) (`split-zone-slice`): Use split-flow action to punish aggressive horizontal pursuit and create a massive cutback alley behind a sealing H-back.. Key conflict: Backside Defensive End (WDE) & Mike Linebacker. Tell cue: Base foundation call: H-Back slices across the formation to kick out the backside DE on true zone run.
  - [Play-Action Dagger Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=pa-dagger-shot) (`pa-dagger-shot`): Exploit aggressive linebacker run fits by pairing a hard split-zone play-action fake with a clear-out post and intermediate Dagger (dig) route.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker & Single-High Free Safety (FS). Tell cue: Backside X stems vertical into intermediate Dagger instead of stalk blocking; QB pulls ball at t=1.3s.
  - [Boot Throwback Y-Leak](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=boot-throwback-leak) (`boot-throwback-leak`): Devastate over-aggressive defenses with the signature Y-Leak constraint: faking a slice block before leaking the H-back vertically into vacated boundary space.. Key conflict: Backside Defensive End (WDE) & Boundary Cornerback (LCB). Tell cue: H-Back bluffs the kick-out block on backside DE and leaks vertically untouched down the sideline.
  - [Orbit Motion Perimeter Toss](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=orbit-motion-toss) (`orbit-motion-toss`): Outflank aggressive defenses by combining pre-snap orbit motion and a rapid perimeter toss with multiple pulling lead blockers.. Key conflict: Strong Safety (SS) & Strongside Defensive End (SDE). Tell cue: Z runs pre-snap orbit motion behind the QB to distort secondary fits before snap.

### Andy Reid's Spread-RPO & Mesh Passing Family (`reid-spread-rpo`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Andy Reid (Kansas City Chiefs)
- **Philosophy**: The pinnacle of modern hybrid football. Andy Reid synthesizes classic West Coast horizontal passing and timed rhythm with modern spread RPO tags, Mesh shallow crossing rub combinations, misdirection power shovel passes, and perimeter sprintout smash-wheel concepts. Operating out of 11-personnel Gun Trips alignments, Reid stresses second-level conflict defenders with identical pre-snap looks before unleashing lethal horizontal and vertical route combinations.
- **Plays**:
  - [Mesh Shallow Cross](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=mesh-shallow-cross) (`mesh-shallow-cross`): Create impossible natural pick/rub traffic for underneath zone and man defenders while stretching the defense horizontally and vertically with perimeter rail and deep clearout routes.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker & Nickel DB (Underneath Hook/Curl defenders). Tell cue: Base mesh timing with RB releasing on a wide rail route while slot receivers execute underneath shallow cross rub.
  - [Inside Zone RPO Glance](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=rpo-glance-post) (`rpo-glance-post`): Put the backside second-level linebacker in an inescapable run-pass conflict, punishing aggressive run fits with immediate intermediate completions.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (Backside Run-Fit Conflict Defender). Tell cue: QB reads backside Will linebacker crashing the B-gap and pulls ball for rapid glance release to X.
  - [Power Shovel Option](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=power-shovel-option) (`power-shovel-option`): Create an unstoppable misdirection interior shovel pass that exploits defensive ends widening to defend the quarterback perimeter option and sweep threat.. Key conflict: Strongside Defensive End (SDE) & Mike Linebacker. Tell cue: Offensive guard pulls frontside while QB executes forward shovel option to TE inserting through A-gap.
  - [Sprintout Smash-Wheel](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=sprintout-smash-wheel) (`sprintout-smash-wheel`): Outflank perimeter pass rush with a moving pocket sprintout while executing a smash-wheel concept that punishes squatting Cover 2 cornerbacks.. Key conflict: Right Cornerback (RCB) & Strong Safety (SS). Tell cue: QB takes half-roll sprintout launch point to perimeter while outside receiver runs high-speed smash-wheel.

### Sean McVay's Condensed Duo & Play-Action Attack (`mcvay-duo-playaction`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Sean McVay (Los Angeles Rams)
- **Philosophy**: Sean McVay's championship offensive system engineered around condensed 11-personnel formations with tight receiver splits. By pairing physical 'Power without a puller' Duo double-teams with identical play-action 3-level Sail floods, explosive deep crossing over-routes, and rapid Glance RPOs, McVay keeps defensive front sevens in permanent schematic conflict.
- **Plays**:
  - [11P Duo Lead Inside Power Run](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcvay-duo-playaction&play=mcvay-duo-lead-run) (`mcvay-duo-lead-run`): Punish light nickel boxes with vertical double-teams ("Duo"), creating massive interior movement and establishing the physical run picture that unlocks play-action shot plays.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Interior LB). Tell cue: Offensive line vertical-punch double teams climbing to Mike linebacker; no pulling guard, RB presses interior A-gap mesh.
  - [Play-Action Sail 3-Level Flood](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcvay-duo-playaction&play=mcvay-pa-sail-flood) (`mcvay-pa-sail-flood`): Create a 3-level vertical flood (deep clearout, 12-yard intermediate out, 2-yard flat) off under-center Duo play-action to overload Cover 3 and Cover 4 zone defenders.. Key conflict: Nickel Apex Defender / Strong Safety (Curl-Flat Defender). Tell cue: Slot receiver H stems vertical before breaking 90 degrees outward on a 12-yard Sail route while QB pulls the ball out of Duo mesh.
  - [Play-Action Deep Over / Crosser](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcvay-duo-playaction&play=mcvay-pa-deep-crosser) (`mcvay-pa-deep-crosser`): Attack the vulnerable intermediate middle-of-the-field void (18-22 yards) against two-high and single-high defenses by pairing a deep post clearout with a crossing over-route.. Key conflict: Weak Safety (FS in Quarters) & Mike Linebacker. Tell cue: Backside X receiver takes a deep inside release crossing behind second-level linebackers at 18-20 yards depth instead of digging or stalk blocking.
  - [Glance RPO with Orbit Return Motion](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcvay-duo-playaction&play=mcvay-glance-rpo-orbit) (`mcvay-glance-rpo-orbit`): Punish aggressive run-stopping linebackers by reading the apex/Will defender on a post-snap RPO, pairing interior Duo power with a rapid Glance slant route.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (Weakside Second-Level Conflict Defender). Tell cue: Pre-snap orbit motion across the backfield paired with post-snap mesh read; QB keeps eyes glued on the conflict apex linebacker.

### Mike McDaniel's Speed Cheat-Motion & Space Attack (`mcdaniel-cheat-motion`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Mike McDaniel (Los Angeles Chargers)
- **Philosophy**: Mike McDaniel's revolutionary speed-in-space scheme that weaponizes pre-snap 'Cheat Motion' (sprint-speed motion at the snap). By giving explosive playmakers a running start to crack edge defenders on perimeter tosses, feigning cracks on devastating sideline wheel shots, punishing overpursuit with inside zone Wham traps, and running pistol speed options in the red zone, McDaniel creates mathematical dilemmas for any defense.
- **Plays**:
  - [Cheat Motion Crack Toss Perimeter Stretch](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcdaniel-cheat-motion&play=mcdaniel-cheat-motion-toss) (`mcdaniel-cheat-motion-toss`): Weaponize extreme pre-snap speed ("Cheat Motion") to create an unmatchable angle on the perimeter, cracking the edge defender and pulling offensive linemen for an explosive outside toss.. Key conflict: SAM Linebacker / Strongside Edge Defender. Tell cue: Receiver in cheat motion snaps inside to deliver crack block on edge/LB while RB takes immediate wide toss track.
  - [Cheat Motion Wheel Shot (Speed Release)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcdaniel-cheat-motion&play=mcdaniel-cheat-motion-wheel) (`mcdaniel-cheat-motion-wheel`): Punish defenses over-committing to McDaniel’s Cheat Motion perimeter crack toss by bluffing the crack block and releasing the fastest receiver on an uncontested vertical wheel route.. Key conflict: Field Cornerback (RCB) & Strong Safety. Tell cue: Motion receiver bluffs crack block for 0.4s then explosive vertical burst along the boundary on the wheel route.
  - [Inside Zone Wham with Cheat Decoy](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcdaniel-cheat-motion&play=mcdaniel-inside-zone-wham) (`mcdaniel-inside-zone-wham`): Exploit defensive lateral overpursuit with an inside zone Wham trap, using pre-snap speed motion as eye candy while trapping the 3-tech DT from the blindside.. Key conflict: 3-Technique Defensive Tackle & Mike Linebacker. Tell cue: FB/H-back cuts back against the grain on a wham trap block on the 3T DT instead of leading to the perimeter.
  - [Pistol Speed Option Pitch & Space Read](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=mcdaniel-cheat-motion&play=mcdaniel-pistol-option-pitch) (`mcdaniel-pistol-option-pitch`): Create a 2-on-1 space dilemma on the perimeter edge in short-yardage / red-zone situations using speed option mechanics from pistol.. Key conflict: Strongside Defensive End (Option Read Key). Tell cue: QB attacks outside shoulder of unblocked DE on a fast lateral option track with RB in parallel pitch relationship.

### Kevin Stefanski's Multi-TE Gap & Under-Center Play-Action Family (`stefanski-multi-te-gap`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Kevin Stefanski (Atlanta Falcons)
- **Philosophy**: Master of condensed multi-tight end structures, violent pin-and-pull gap schemes, GT counter lead concepts, and deep play-action seam/bootleg shots. Kevin Stefanski builds an overpowering offensive machine founded on angle blocking, devastating complementary under-center fakes, and high-efficiency vertical passing off run action.
- **Plays**:
  - [13P Pin & Pull Sweep](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=stefanski-multi-te-gap&play=stefanski-pin-pull-sweep) (`stefanski-pin-pull-sweep`): Create overwhelming perimeter gap leverage against single-high defenses by pinning frontside defensive linemen inside and pulling interior linemen as lead escorts.. Key conflict: Strong Safety (SS) & Mike Linebacker (MIKE). Tell cue: Center & RG immediately pull playside while RT & Y down-block (pin).
  - [Play-Action Seam Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=stefanski-multi-te-gap&play=stefanski-pa-seam-shot) (`stefanski-pa-seam-shot`): Punish aggressive single-high run defenses by faking the pin-and-pull sweep and launching a vertical seam strike to the primary tight end behind suckered linebackers and safeties.. Key conflict: Free Safety (FS) & Strong Safety (SS). Tell cue: Y releases vertically after flash down-block; QB sets deep in pocket instead of handing off.
  - [Naked Bootleg Slide](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=stefanski-multi-te-gap&play=stefanski-naked-boot-slide) (`stefanski-naked-boot-slide`): Exploit defenses over-pursuing Stefanski's heavy pin-and-pull run flow by rolling the quarterback naked to the opposite boundary with a 3-level flood/slide concept.. Key conflict: Weakside Defensive End (WDE) & Will Linebacker (WILL). Tell cue: QB keeps ball around backside edge naked; backside TE (U) releases into weakside flat.
  - [Counter Gap GT Lead](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=stefanski-multi-te-gap&play=stefanski-counter-gap-lead) (`stefanski-counter-gap-lead`): Gasoline the defense with heavy gap-scheme power: down blocks create an unmovable wall, while a pulling guard kicks out the edge and a lead tight end pancakes the linebacker.. Key conflict: Strongside Defensive End (SDE) & Mike Linebacker (MIKE). Tell cue: Backside LG and F pull across formation on GT/GF counter paths; RB takes counter jab step before cutting back.

### Shane Steichen's QB Mesh & Spread RPO System (`steichen-qb-mesh-rpo`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Shane Steichen (Indianapolis Colts)
- **Philosophy**: A dual-threat quarterback maximization system rooted in Andy Reid's West Coast principles with modern college Spread DNA. Shane Steichen pairs zone-read power runs with RPO bubble/glance perimeter reads, Mesh shallow crosses that create natural rubs against man coverage, and vertical switch releases that exploit deep zone voids. The system demands a mobile signal-caller who threatens the edge on every designed run, compressing defensive end responsibilities into an impossible choice.
- **Plays**:
  - [Gun QB Power Read](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-qb-power-read) (`steichen-qb-power-read`): Put the frontside defensive end in an impossible spatial dilemma: if he widens to stop the perimeter sweep, the dual-threat QB powers downhill behind a pulling guard.. Key conflict: Strongside Defensive End (SDE) & Mike Linebacker (MIKE). Tell cue: Backside RG pulls playside while RB crosses on horizontal sweep path; QB reads frontside DE.
  - [Mesh Rail / Wheel](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-mesh-rail-wheel) (`steichen-mesh-rail-wheel`): Exploit man-to-man coverage by pairing a tight shallow-cross Mesh rub with an explosive running back Rail/Wheel route along the boundary.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (WILL) & Free Safety (FS). Tell cue: RB free-releases on boundary rail/wheel route while slot receivers set tight crossing rub.
  - [Inside Zone + Bubble Screen RPO](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-zone-bubble-rpo) (`steichen-zone-bubble-rpo`): Conflict the apex/overhang defender with a simultaneous inside zone run and perimeter bubble screen, taking whatever the defense concedes with ruthless efficiency.. Key conflict: Nickel DB (Overhang Conflict Key). Tell cue: Playside WRs immediately stalk block on snap while slot WR flares on bubble arc; QB catches and throws at mesh.
  - [4-Verticals Switch Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-verticals-switch) (`steichen-verticals-switch`): Destroy Two-High Quarters coverage by crossing the release paths of the #1 and #2 receivers on deep vertical tracks, triggering coverage miscommunication and blown assignments.. Key conflict: Strong Safety (SS) & Right Cornerback (RCB). Tell cue: Slot H and outside Z cross stems at 6 yards on vertical release instead of standard screen/blocking releases.

### Matt LaFleur's Illusion of Complexity & Deep Shot Family (`lafleur-illusion-packers`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Matt LaFleur (Green Bay Packers)
- **Philosophy**: A masterclass in schematic deception and visual illusion. Matt LaFleur marries condensed 12-personnel and dual-back Pony sets with identical under-center wide-zone run mechanics to lull defenses into overpursuing, before unlocking catastrophic deep Cross-Country Posts, Dagger intermediate concepts, and perimeter constraint wheels.
- **Plays**:
  - [Wide Zone Cutback (Illusion Flow)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lafleur-illusion-packers&play=lafleur-wide-zone-cutback) (`lafleur-wide-zone-cutback`): Create wide horizontal stretch with 12-personnel under-center flow to force linebackers to overpursue and open a devastating backside cutback lane.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Flow Linebacker). Tell cue: Full offensive line lateral bucket steps with under-center RB taking the handoff and pressing the tackle landmark rather than QB keeping.
  - [PA Cross-Country Deep Post](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lafleur-illusion-packers&play=lafleur-cross-country-post) (`lafleur-cross-country-post`): Present an identical wide-zone run look to pull linebackers downhill and manipulate the single-high Free Safety with an intermediate crosser, opening an explosive deep post across the entire field.. Key conflict: Free Safety (Deep Middle Cover 3 Safety). Tell cue: Tight end (TE1) releasing into the secondary after a 0.8-second delay rather than staying attached to the perimeter reach block.
  - [Pony Package Screen-Wheel Constraint](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lafleur-illusion-packers&play=lafleur-pony-screen-wheel) (`lafleur-pony-screen-wheel`): Exploit defenses overreacting to quick perimeter screen calls by pairing dual-back Pony personnel with a fake screen left and a devastating rail wheel right.. Key conflict: Apex Nickel / Strong Safety (Boundary Flat & Deep Half Defenders). Tell cue: Shotgun Pony split-back alignment with QB pump-faking to the swing before resetting his feet to the opposite boundary.
  - [PA Dagger Seam-Dig Concept](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lafleur-illusion-packers&play=lafleur-pa-dagger-dig) (`lafleur-pa-dagger-dig`): Attack 2-high / Cover 4 Quarters defenses using a two-man vertical stretch (Seam Pin + 15-yard Dig) over an underneath shallow drag crosser.. Key conflict: Middle Linebacker & Quarters Free Safety. Tell cue: Tight bunch alignment with TE1 bursting vertically up the seam rather than crossing behind the line of scrimmage.

### Nick Sirianni's Power RPO & Brotherly Shove System (`sirianni-power-rpo`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Nick Sirianni (Philadelphia Eagles)
- **Philosophy**: A physical, identity-driven offense built on gap power football paired with perimeter RPO access. Nick Sirianni's Eagles combine power duo runs that rely on vertical double-teams, RPO glance and slant reads that punish aggressive linebackers, boundary isolation for elite wide receivers, and the most famous short-yardage play in the NFL — the Brotherly Shove quarterback sneak.
- **Plays**:
  - [Inside Power Duo (Double Teams)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=sirianni-power-rpo&play=sirianni-power-duo-inside) (`sirianni-power-duo-inside`): Impose pure physical will at the line of scrimmage with interior Duo double teams, blowing defensive tackles off the ball and creating a heavy north-south running lane.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (Interior Gap Fitter). Tell cue: Gun 3x1 formation with offensive line firing straight ahead on vertical power angles without pulling guards.
  - [Backside Glance ISO RPO](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=sirianni-power-rpo&play=sirianni-rpo-glance-iso) (`sirianni-rpo-glance-iso`): Put the backside Will linebacker in an impossible run-pass conflict: if he steps up to stop the interior Duo run, punish him immediately with a rapid Glance route to the isolated X receiver.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (Backside Conflict / Run-Fit LB). Tell cue: Quarterback keeping eyes locked on the backside linebacker during the mesh rather than carrying out a naked keeper.
  - [Slot Fade Out Isolation](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=sirianni-power-rpo&play=sirianni-slot-fade-out) (`sirianni-slot-fade-out`): Create an isolated 1-on-1 matchup on the perimeter for an elite route-runner from the slot, using an underneath out route to pin the outside corner and clear the sideline.. Key conflict: Star / Nickel Defensive Back (Inside Leverage Slot Defender). Tell cue: Straight dropback by the QB from 2x2 formation with no mesh handoff action.
  - [Brotherly Shove (Tush Push)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=sirianni-power-rpo&play=sirianni-qb-sneak-push) (`sirianni-qb-sneak-push`): Execute the mathematically and physically near-unstoppable short-yardage quarterback sneak by combining low offensive line pad leverage with dual backfield pushers.. Key conflict: Nose Tackles & Mike Linebacker (Interior Goal-Line Squeeze). Tell cue: Ultra-tight wedge splits along the offensive line with dual pushers aligned directly behind the quarterback’s hips.

### Ben Johnson's Counter Deception & Gadget Offense (`johnson-counter-deception`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Ben Johnson (Detroit Lions)
- **Philosophy**: A brilliantly layered offensive system built on counter run misdirection, pre-snap orbit motion, and seamless play-action packaging. Ben Johnson weaponizes dual-pull counters, hook-ladder mesh rubs, TE throwback leaks off counter PA, and orbit-driven RB screen convoys to create a complete deception ecosystem where every play looks identical from the defensive perspective until it's too late.
- **Plays**:
  - [11P Gun Counter Trey Lead (Detroit Back-Side Deception)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=johnson-counter-deception&play=johnson-counter-trey-lead) (`johnson-counter-trey-lead`): Use pre-snap counter step and dual pulling guard deception to freeze linebackers and create an explosive B-gap crease.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside LB). Tell cue: Both guards pull simultaneously in same direction; RB counter false step with QB reverse pivot before handoff.
  - [Play-Action TE Throwback Leak (Counter Shell PA)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=johnson-counter-deception&play=johnson-pa-te-throwback) (`johnson-pa-te-throwback`): Use counter run look PA to move WILL linebacker inside, then throw back to leaking TE in the vacated flat.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (Weakside LB). Tell cue: Same counter step from RB and reverse pivot from QB — but TE releases instead of blocking at 0.8s.
  - [Hook-Ladder Mesh with TE Stack (Quick Deception Screen)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=johnson-counter-deception&play=johnson-hook-ladder-mesh) (`johnson-hook-ladder-mesh`): Exploit man-coverage rules with a 2-man mesh rub that legally frees the RB against press-man Nickel coverage on 3rd down.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (Man Coverage on RB). Tell cue: TE aligned tight to line at tackle depth; RB initial release toward TE before sharp angle to mesh.
  - [Orbit Reverse Screen with Late Wheel Release (Detroit Gadget)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=johnson-counter-deception&play=johnson-orbit-reverse-screen) (`johnson-orbit-reverse-screen`): Use orbit motion and deep QB look-off to pull all defenders deep and inside, then dump to RB with three escort blockers in the flat.. Key conflict: Strong Safety (Deep TE Wheel Responsibility). Tell cue: Orbit motion pre-snap with TE crossing behind QB; three linemen releasing early is the screen key.

### Sean Payton's Quick Game & Screen Package (`payton-quick-game-screens`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Sean Payton (Denver Broncos)
- **Philosophy**: A rhythm-first quick game built to beat man-match leverage and punish over-aggressive fronts before pressure can develop. Payton layers slant-flat rhythm throws, convoy fast screens, and interior shovel tunnels beneath jet-sweep play action — every call attacks the defender who triggers first, and every screen looks like protection until the geometry springs.
- **Plays**:
  - [Quick Game Slant-Flat Rhythm](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=payton-quick-game-screens&play=payton-slant-flat-rhythm) (`payton-slant-flat-rhythm`): Force the apex defender into an instant flat-vs-slant leverage decision and attack the answer he does not pick, on a one-hitch rhythm clock.. Key conflict: Nickel Corner (apex over H). Tell cue: The NICKEL opens flat-side at 0.5s while Z stems outside then cuts the slant behind his shoulders — the ball is gone before the RCB re-establishes.
  - [Fast Screen Convoy Right](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=payton-quick-game-screens&play=payton-fast-screen-convoy) (`payton-fast-screen-convoy`): Get the ball to the perimeter instantly, before any rush or coverage reaction can develop, and let a two-man convoy block the only defenders who trigger correctly.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (screen-side chaser). Tell cue: The ball is out at ~0.6s with zero route development, and the TE plus slot sprint into blocking arcs instead of routes — pure convoy geometry.
  - [Tunnel Screen Shovel Package](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=payton-quick-game-screens&play=payton-tunnel-shovel-package) (`payton-tunnel-shovel-package`): Build an interior blocking tunnel between the guards, shovel the ball to a full-speed crossing receiver at its mouth, and outrun a defense that triggered on run and false-screen looks.. Key conflict: 3-technique Defensive Tackle (rush lane vs shovel window). Tell cue: H crosses behind the line and disappears between the two guards while Z sprints under the formation — nobody runs a route beyond eight yards.
  - [Jet Sweep PA Deep Post](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=payton-quick-game-screens&play=payton-jet-sweep-pa-post) (`payton-jet-sweep-pa-post`): Use full-field jet sweep action to pull both linebackers and the free safety downhill, then hit a deep post behind the displaced coverage.. Key conflict: Free Safety. Tell cue: Z carries a true full-field sweep path across the formation while X stems outside then stacks a deep post — the only deep route on the call.

### Greg Roman's Power Read & QB Run Attack (`roman-power-read`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Greg Roman (Los Angeles Chargers)
- **Philosophy**: The most quarterback-centric gap-scheme system in modern football, built on heavy 22 personnel and the unblocked-read-key geometry that made Lamar Jackson an MVP. Greg Roman packages power read pulls, designed QB power keepers, pin-and-pull perimeter leverage, and identical-picture play-action shots so that every defensive run fit is simultaneously a pass-fit decision — and heavy personnel becomes an offensive weapon instead of a tell.
- **Plays**:
  - [Power Read Pull (Keep off the Crashing End)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=roman-power-read&play=roman-power-read-pull) (`roman-power-read-pull`): Put the unblocked playside defensive end in an impossible choice between the RB's flow and the QB's keep, then punish the crash with a pulling guard and fullback lead.. Key conflict: Playside Defensive End (Read Key) — unblocked SDE. Tell cue: The QB rides the mesh with eyes locked on the unblocked end instead of securing the handoff — if that end crashes, the ball never leaves.
  - [QB Power (Keeper Behind the Pull)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=roman-power-read&play=roman-qb-power-run) (`roman-qb-power-run`): Run true QB power with no read: use the fullback to wrong-arm the unblocked edge and the pulling guard to log the Mike, handing the quarterback a designed crease in the B/C-gap.. Key conflict: Unblocked Edge Defender — forced to wrong-arm into the FB kick-out. Tell cue: There is no read and no extended mesh — the QB clamps the ball at the snap and the fullback kicks the first color he sees.
  - [Pin & Pull Leverage Sweep](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=roman-power-read&play=roman-pin-pull-leverage) (`roman-pin-pull-leverage`): Attack the perimeter's leverage math: pin every down defender with interior blockers, then outnumber the edge with tandem pulling guards, a fullback, and an arcing wing.. Key conflict: Force Player (SAM) — caught between spilling the sweep and boxing the edge. Tell cue: Both guards pull together around four stationary pins while the QB hands and boots away — no mesh read, no decision, pure numbers sweep.
  - [Heavy Personnel PA Deep Post Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=roman-power-read&play=roman-pa-post-shot) (`roman-pa-post-shot`): Weaponize the established Power Read Pull picture — same mesh, same pull, same lead — to bait the single-high safety downhill and take a deep post shot behind him.. Key conflict: Free Safety — single-high defender who must honor heavy-run action or the deep middle. Tell cue: The backfield is a perfect copy of Power Read Pull, but X never blocks — his vertical release off the snap is the one frame that gives it away.

### Kevin O'Connell's Boot & Dagger Play-Action System (`oconnell-boot-dagger`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Kevin O'Connell (Minnesota Vikings)
- **Philosophy**: A play-action ecosystem where every call wears the same uniform: a condensed gun formation that produces an identical wide-zone reach wash and mesh point for the first full second of every snap. The stretch base establishes the picture, the boot flood punishes flow-away defenders, the Dagger seam-curl attacks the dropping Mike, and the duo PA crosser exploits downhill triggers — four answers off one visual lie.
- **Plays**:
  - [Condensed Wide-Zone Stretch Base](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=oconnell-boot-dagger&play=oconnell-wide-zone-stretch-base) (`oconnell-wide-zone-stretch-base`): Establish the pure wide-zone stretch picture that every boot, dagger, and crosser companion in the family borrows from.. Key conflict: Playside flow linebacker (MIKE). Tell cue: The ball actually goes to the back — no boot pivot, no pocket reset; the QB's ride ends in a carried-out fake rather than a throw.
  - [Wide-Zone Boot Flood](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=oconnell-boot-dagger&play=oconnell-boot-flood-rollout) (`oconnell-boot-flood-rollout`): Punish the defensive flow created by the base stretch by pulling the QB against the grain into a three-level boundary flood.. Key conflict: Backside contain EDGE and flow-away flat defender (WILL). Tell cue: The QB's ride turns into a reverse pivot against the flow — linemen keep blocking stretch right while the ball-carrier disappears left.
  - [PA Dagger Seam-Curl Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=oconnell-boot-dagger&play=oconnell-pa-dagger-shot) (`oconnell-pa-dagger-shot`): Use the stretch-action pocket reset to attack the middle of Cover 3 Sky with a Dagger — seam above, curl in the void behind the dropping MLB.. Key conflict: MIKE (hook-to-curl conflict). Tell cue: The QB never leaves the pocket — the ride ends in a hitch-and-reset rather than a handoff, a boot pivot, or a carried-out fake.
  - [Duo PA Boundary Crosser](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=oconnell-boot-dagger&play=oconnell-duo-pa-crosser) (`oconnell-duo-pa-crosser`): Pair a downhill duo run fake with a free backside crosser to punish linebackers and cornerbacks who trigger on run action.. Key conflict: SAM / backside apex. Tell cue: The RB plants downhill instead of pressing the perimeter — OL blockers converge into a vertical double team rather than washing laterally.

### Liam Coen's Hybrid Wide-Zone RPO System (`coen-wide-zone-rpo`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Liam Coen (Jacksonville Jaguars)
- **Philosophy**: The modern evolution of the Shanahan-McVay tree: Liam Coen packages genuine wide-zone run mechanics directly with post-snap RPOs, turning every zone-stretch call into a triple-option math problem for the defense. Glance shots off box-number reads, three-level bubble-slant-flat triangles, cross-field crack tosses, and orbit-motion cutbacks all grow from the same identical run picture — the defense can never be right against both halves of any call.
- **Plays**:
  - [Wide-Zone + Glance RPO (Box-Number Read)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coen-wide-zone-rpo&play=coen-wide-zone-glance-rpo) (`coen-wide-zone-glance-rpo`): Package wide-zone run mechanics with a post-snap glance so the QB can hand off or throw based purely on how the apex nickel defends the box.. Key conflict: NICKEL (apex run-fit vs RPO conflict). Tell cue: Identical run-flow picture until the nickel commits — then the ball comes out over his head instead of going into the RB's belly.
  - [Bubble-Slant-Flat Triangle RPO (Zone-Read Action)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coen-wide-zone-rpo&play=coen-bubble-triangle-rpo) (`coen-bubble-triangle-rpo`): Turn one zone-read call into a true triple-option math problem by stretching a single apex defender with three simultaneous targets at three depths.. Key conflict: NICKEL or SS (apex squeezed three ways). Tell cue: Three receivers release at three distinct depths off zone-read ride action — bubble arc, inside slant, and chasing TE flat — instead of any single downfield route tree.
  - [Crack-Toss Perimeter Attack (X Cracks the Force)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coen-wide-zone-rpo&play=coen-crack-toss-perimeter) (`coen-crack-toss-perimeter`): Attack soft-force perimeter rules with speed toss plus a cross-field crack, making the force defender choose between an uncovered crack blocker and the alley he must fill.. Key conflict: Force defender cracked by X (the nickel). Tell cue: Backside X sprints cross-field on a visible max-effort crack angle while the line's footwork points the opposite way from the eventual toss.
  - [Motion-Declared Zone Cutback (Orbit Drag)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coen-wide-zone-rpo&play=coen-motion-zone-cutback) (`coen-motion-zone-cutback`): Use pre-snap orbit motion to interrogate and declare the overhang's run fit, then punish the resulting flow commitment with a wide-zone cutback into the vacated backside seam.. Key conflict: Backside WILL (cutback fit). Tell cue: H crosses the formation in orbit at the snap and never runs a route — he settles and climbs into a lead block while the RB visibly bends backward against the stretch flow.

### Chip Kelly's Tempo Spread & Air Raid System (`kelly-tempo-spread`)
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Chip Kelly (Las Vegas Raiders)
- **Philosophy**: A snap-rate offense built to make defensive communication the first conflict on every play: Kelly snaps within seconds of the previous whistle, denying substitutions and rotations before the ball is even live. The system layers classic Air Raid spacing — Mesh rubs and Spot stress — over a spread-option run game whose zone-read/draw geometry breaks box math, then punishes two-high shells with four-verts takeoffs off a simple pre-snap MOFO read.
- **Plays**:
  - [Mesh Spacing Concept at Tempo](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kelly-tempo-spread&play=kelly-mesh-spacing-concept) (`kelly-mesh-spacing-concept`): Weaponize tempo and classic Air Raid spacing — two shallow crossers rubbing under the quarterback with corners and over routes stacked behind — to stress man coverage's navigation rules and zone coverage's hook depth.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (navigating crossing trash). Tell cue: Both inside slots exchange full-field shallow crossers directly under the QB within a second of the previous whistle — zero huddle, zero pre-snap motion.
  - [Three-Level Spot Stress](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kelly-tempo-spread&play=kelly-spot-tempo-stress) (`kelly-spot-tempo-stress`): Layer flat, spot/curl, and vertical takeoff off one shoulder so the apex nickel must defend three landmarks with two responsibilities, then beat the rotation clock with a one-hitch rhythm throw.. Key conflict: Nickel (flat/curl conflict). Tell cue: H freezes in a catcher-box spot at exactly five yards with the RB flat swinging under and X clearing over the top — every other receiver leaves the picture immediately.
  - [Zone-Read RB Draw Package](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kelly-tempo-spread&play=kelly-zone-read-rb-draw) (`kelly-zone-read-rb-draw`): Pair the zone-read's unblocked-end geometry with an RB delayed draw so the defense's box math commits to a play flowing one way while the ball hits a vacated gap going the other.. Key conflict: Unblocked read-key DE and the WILL fitting the draw. Tell cue: RB presses wide-zone right for two steps, then sinks his hips and snaps back into the backside B-gap — the mid-play hip turn at the mesh point is the only visual cue.
  - [Four Verts Takeover vs Two-High](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=kelly-tempo-spread&play=kelly-four-verts-takeover) (`kelly-four-verts-takeover`): Attack a two-high shell's structural weakness — the open middle third — with four simultaneous verticals and sideline takes, letting the pre-snap MOFO read dictate a seam shot before the safeties can squeeze.. Key conflict: Middle-third/match safety. Tell cue: All four receivers release vertically off the snap with sideline takes and zero intermediate cuts — the QB’s eyes lock on the MOFO window before anyone breaks.

### Don Coryell's Air Coryell Vertical Family (`coryell-vertical`) — Era: `past-nfl`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Don Coryell (San Diego Chargers (1978-86))
- **Philosophy**: The original vertical passing tree. Coryell stretched defenses with five-step drops, seam-post strokes, and layered deep crossers, forcing single-high safeties to defend the whole field while tight ends occupied the middle hole. Every modern timing-based passing game descends from these four calls.
- **Plays**:
  - [Seam-Post Double Stroke](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-seam-post-double-stroke) (`coryell-seam-post-double-stroke`): Attack the deep middle with two synchronized seam-post strokes that force the single-high safety to pick a side.. Key conflict: Free Safety (middle-third defender). Tell cue: Both outside receivers take identical vertical stems before breaking — the stroke only happens after the stems have sold pure fades.
  - [Deep Out & Comeback](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-deep-out-comeback) (`coryell-deep-out-comeback`): Force a press corner to defend two throws at one landmark: the 18-yard deep out first, then the 16-yard comeback.. Key conflict: Right Corner (press corner on the flanker). Tell cue: The flanker runs a pure vertical stem past twelve yards before any break — the throw is always late-breaking at the top of the route.
  - [Cross-Country Drag Series](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-cross-country-drag) (`coryell-cross-country-drag`): Flood the middle of the field with two staggered deep crossers so zone drops cannot cover both layers.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle hook drop). Tell cue: Both inside receivers release instantly vertical and only break after passing twelve yards — shallow drags never appear in this series.
  - [Z-Snap Move Screen](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-z-snap-move-screen) (`coryell-z-snap-move-screen`): Punish Cover 2 flat defenders who sit on the short routes created by the vertical passing game.. Key conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong-flat defender). Tell cue: Z's alignment move happens before the ball is out of the quarterback's hand — a true vertical shot has no pre-break stem move.

### Bill Walsh's Classic West Coast Offense (`walsh-classic-wco`) — Era: `past-nfl`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Bill Walsh (San Francisco 49ers (1979-88))
- **Philosophy**: The timing-and-leverage passing system that replaced the vertical bomb with surgical rhythm throws designed to run like the sweep. Every call answers a leverage question in under two seconds, and every answer sets up the next question through sequencing.
- **Plays**:
  - [Slant-Flat Combo](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-slant-flat-combo) (`walsh-slant-flat-combo`): Turn an off-coverage corner's cushion into free yardage with a timed slant-flat stretch.. Key conflict: Right Corner (Cover 2 flat defender). Tell cue: The flanker releases flat on his first step and the ball is out within 1.2 seconds — anything slower means the defense triggered correctly.
  - [Sprint Right Option](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-sprint-right-option) (`walsh-sprint-right-option`): Use the sprint to displace the entire defense horizontally so the primary corner route or the naked flat checkdown comes open.. Key conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong-flat defender). Tell cue: The quarterback leaves the launch point horizontally within half a second — no drop step ever occurs.
  - [Curl-Flat Flood](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-curl-flat-flood) (`walsh-curl-flat-flood`): Vertically stretch one flat defender with three routes at three depths until he must give up a leg of the flood.. Key conflict: Right Corner (Cover 3 sky flat dropper). Tell cue: All three flood legs release to one side within the first second — a true flood never distributes to both sides.
  - [Play-Action Deep Cross](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-play-action-deep-cross) (`walsh-play-action-deep-cross`): Exploit the slant-flat success by freezing the second-level defenders with run action and shooting the vacated middle.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (run-fit linebacker). Tell cue: The fullback crosses the line of scrimmage carrying the fake — on the real slant-flat he never leaves the pocket.

### June Jones's Run and Shoot (`run-and-shoot`) — Era: `past-nfl`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: June Jones (Houston Oilers (1989-93) / Hawaii)
- **Philosophy**: Four-wide spread passing built on read routes instead of fixed breaks. Every receiver carries a conversion rule keyed to defender leverage, so the same four calls attack man, zone, and blitz differently. The Oilers' run-and-shoot stretched single-high shells with switch releases, mesh traffic, and perimeter wheels — the direct ancestor of modern spacing-option passing games.
- **Plays**:
  - [Switch Verticals vs Man](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-switch-verticals) (`rns-switch-verticals`): Force man-coverage defenders into crossed releases that convert into a two-man rub, freeing a vertical behind single-high coverage.. Key conflict: Free Safety (last line in man free). Tell cue: The releases cross below four yards before either stem develops — a true double-vertical keeps both receivers on parallel outside tracks.
  - [Mesh Read-Route](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-mesh-read-route) (`rns-mesh-read-route`): Create a natural rub with two shallow crossers and let each receiver convert off the defender's leverage rather than a fixed break point.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle-hole wall). Tell cue: The crossers never stop until they feel a defender's leverage — a called mesh with set breaks settles at the same spot every snap regardless of coverage.
  - [Post-Wheel Leverage Read](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-post-wheel-leverage-read) (`rns-post-wheel-leverage-read`): Punish soft bail coverage by selling a post stem and converting into a wheel that attacks the vacated outside third behind the corner's back.. Key conflict: Left Corner (soft bail with eyes on QB). Tell cue: The receiver plants off an inside stem and accelerates away from the numbers — a called post never leaves its diagonal track.
  - [Go-Route Stab Adjustment](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-go-route-stab) (`rns-go-route-stab`): Use the outside go as bait for a bailing corner and convert the inside stab into a climb that attacks the vacated seam between the coverage levels.. Key conflict: Right Corner (bail technique with back to the slot). Tell cue: The slot plants at six yards before accelerating — a called seam or vertical never breaks stride below eight.

### Paul Johnson's Flexbone Triple Option (`flexbone-triple-option`) — Era: `current-college`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Paul Johnson (Georgia Tech / Navy)
- **Philosophy**: The modern flexbone: two slotbacks in pitch relationships, a fullback on the midline, and a quarterback who reads one unblocked defender per snap. Every call is a math problem — dive, keep, or pitch — and the defense must be right three times to stop it once. Paul Johnson's Georgia Tech and Navy teams turned this into college football's most efficient rushing attack.
- **Plays**:
  - [Midline Triple Option](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-midline-triple) (`flexbone-midline-triple`): Attack the interior read defender with a three-phase conflict — take the dive and lose the keeper, squeeze the keeper and surrender the pitch.. Key conflict: 3-Tech Defensive Tackle (unblocked dive-read key). Tell cue: The dive hits the exact midline of the guard-center gap and the quarterback reads an interior defender — veer reads the end instead.
  - [Rocket Toss Pitch Series](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-rocket-toss-pitch) (`flexbone-rocket-toss-pitch`): Attack the perimeter with a full-speed motion back so the pitch arrives at maximum velocity before the defense can reset its force geometry.. Key conflict: Strong Safety (perimeter force player). Tell cue: The pitch is extended laterally to a moving back at full speed — option triples hand or ride stationary before reading.
  - [Inside Veer Triple](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-inside-veer-triple) (`flexbone-inside-veer-triple`): Make the playside end choose between the dive and the keep, then punish any third defender who joins with the pitch phase.. Key conflict: Playside Defensive End (unblocked read key). Tell cue: The dive aims at the B-gap behind the down-blocked tackle and the read is the wide end — midline reads interior and dives at the guard-center seam.
  - [Midline Play-Action Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-midline-play-action-shot) (`flexbone-midline-play-action-shot`): Weaponize the triple-option run identity to vacate the deep middle, then attack it with a post shot off an identical midline fake.. Key conflict: Free Safety (middle-third defender). Tell cue: The slot releases upfield instead of running a pitch track, and the tackle arcs then resets to pass set — live option plays never do either.

### Mike Leach's Air Raid Family (`air-raid`) — Era: `current-college`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Mike Leach (Texas Tech / Washington State / Mississippi State)
- **Philosophy**: The purest expression of spread passing: a handful of simple, repeatable concepts thrown from gun at high volume. Every play answers one leverage question, and the quarterback is taught to throw the open receiver rather than force landmarks.
- **Plays**:
  - [Mesh Concept](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-mesh-concept) (`airraid-mesh-concept`): Create guaranteed separation against man coverage through two crossing shallow routes that naturally screen each other's defenders.. Key conflict: Nickel (defender on the inside slot). Tell cue: Both inside receivers take identical one-step vertical fakes before breaking at exactly six yards.
  - [Y-Cross](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-y-cross) (`airraid-y-cross`): Use the stick as bait to occupy the nickel and Will, then attack the vacated middle with the tight end's twelve-yard crosser.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle hook dropper). Tell cue: The tight end releases inside immediately — on mesh both crossers come from slots; here only one crosser ever appears.
  - [Stick-Naked Constraint](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-stick-naked-constraint) (`airraid-stick-naked-constraint`): Double-cover the stick deliberately so the naked swing constraint runs free behind over-committed flat defenders.. Key conflict: Sam Linebacker (weak-flat defender). Tell cue: The running back never blocks — he releases across the backfield on his first step, which no true stick play does.
  - [Shallow Distribution Drive](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-shallow-distribution-drive) (`airraid-shallow-distribution-drive`): Distribute the ball to whichever shallow receiver wins his individual leverage race, reading defenders rather than landmarks.. Key conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle hook dropper). Tell cue: The two crossers never converge at one point — they stay four yards apart in depth for the entire route.

### Tubby Raymond's Delaware Wing-T (`delaware-wing-t`) — Era: `past-college`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Harold "Tubby" Raymond (Delaware (1966-2001))
- **Philosophy**: The Delaware Wing-T is a series-based system where every play looks identical for the first two steps. Guard-pull Buck Sweep forces the perimeter to defend numbers it does not have, and Waggle, Counter Crisscross, and the Wingback Trap all feed off that single picture. Tubby Raymond ran this offense at Delaware for thirty-five years, winning three national championships.
- **Plays**:
  - [Buck Sweep w/ Guard Pull](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-buck-sweep-guard-pull) (`wingt-buck-sweep-guard-pull`): Get two blockers on the perimeter before the ball carrier arrives, collapsing contain inward so the sweep can turn upfield.. Key conflict: Right Corner (perimeter force player). Tell cue: Both guards leave their gaps at the same instant — no other Wing-T series moves both interior linemen horizontally on the snap.
  - [Waggle Pass Off Sweep Fake](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-waggle-flood) (`wingt-waggle-flood`): Use the most convincing run action in football to move an entire defense one direction, then attack the vacated half with a three-level flood.. Key conflict: Free Safety (deep middle). Tell cue: The quarterback reverses direction after the mesh instead of extending the handoff — live sweeps never send the ball carrier and passer to opposite halves.
  - [Counter Crisscross](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-counter-crisscross) (`wingt-counter-crisscross`): Exploit Buck Sweep's tendency with an opposite-direction counter whose backfield action crossfaces every flow defender.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (flow reader). Tell cue: The quarterback reverses his shoulder mid-play to hand off backward — live sweeps and boots never change the ballcarrier after the initial mesh.
  - [Wingback Trap-Gut](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-wingback-trap-gut) (`wingt-wingback-trap-gut`): Punish aggressive interior slants by trapping the penetrating lineman under complete Buck Sweep disguise.. Key conflict: 3-Tech Defensive Tackle (slanting trap target). Tell cue: The playside guard pulls flat then reverses direction mid-step — true sweep pullers never come back to the interior.

### Vince Lombardi's T-Formation Power Sweep (`t-formation-power-sweep`) — Era: `past-nfl`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Vince Lombardi (Green Bay Packers (1959-67))
- **Philosophy**: The most sequenced run system in football history. The double-pull sweep ran dozens of times a game, and every companion play — counter-boot, fullback blast, and flood bootleg — borrowed its exact picture so defenses could never trust what they saw.
- **Plays**:
  - [Power Sweep Left](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-power-sweep-left) (`sweep-power-sweep-left`): Run outside the tackles behind two pulling guards so the defense's edge structure collapses inward and the perimeter belongs to the offense.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (weak-side flow linebacker). Tell cue: Two linemen leave the line of scrimmage immediately in opposite directions — no Lombardi companion play shows this picture.
  - [Power Sweep Right w/ Boot Fake](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-power-sweep-right-boot-fake) (`sweep-power-sweep-right-boot-fake`): Use the sweep's identical picture to drag all eleven defenders right, then attack the abandoned backside with a counter-bootleg.. Key conflict: Free Safety (split-field safety). Tell cue: The quarterback keeps the ball after the mesh — on the true sweep he is empty-handed within one step.
  - [Fullback Blast](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-fullback-blast) (`sweep-fullback-blast`): Punish defenses that over-play the sweep by handing to the fullback between the tackles off identical footwork.. Key conflict: Will Linebacker (flow linebacker). Tell cue: The fullback takes the ball instead of leading it — every true sweep shows the fullback blocking on the perimeter.
  - [Sweep-Pass Bootleg](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-sweep-pass-bootleg) (`sweep-sweep-pass-bootleg`): Convert sweep credibility into a moving-pocket flood throw against defenders frozen by run fits.. Key conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong-hook defender). Tell cue: The tight end releases vertically instead of blocking — no true Lombardi sweep shows an end running a pass route.

### Chris Ault's Pistol Read-Option (`pistol-read-option`) — Era: `past-college`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Chris Ault (Nevada Wolf Pack)
- **Philosophy**: The Pistol marries gun spacing with under-center run physics: the quarterback lines up four yards deep with the back directly behind him, so every zone and gap run hits downhill at full pad level while still carrying a quarterback keep threat. Chris Ault invented the formation at Nevada, where Colin Kaepernick turned it into a 2,000-yard rushing attack.
- **Plays**:
  - [Pistol Inside Zone Read](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-inside-zone-read) (`pistol-inside-zone-read`): Put the backside end in an instant give-or-keep conflict using downhill pistol run physics.. Key conflict: Backside Defensive End (unblocked read key). Tell cue: The running back is directly behind the quarterback at six yards and hits the line downhill — gun reads develop a half-yard deeper.
  - [Pistol Power-O Read](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-power-o-read) (`pistol-power-o-read`): Combine gap-scheme power blocking with a read of the backside end so the defense must defend both the pull and the keep.. Key conflict: Backside Defensive End (unblocked read key). Tell cue: A guard pulls while the quarterback still reads a defender — pure power-o hands the ball immediately with no ride phase.
  - [Pistol PA Deep Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-pa-deep-shot) (`pistol-pa-deep-shot`): Weaponize the pistol run identity to vacate the deep middle, then attack it with a post shot off a half-roll.. Key conflict: Free Safety (middle-third defender). Tell cue: The slot releases across the formation instead of arcing to kick a linebacker, and the line finishes with pass-set feet — live runs never do either.
  - [Pistol Speed Option](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-speed-option) (`pistol-speed-option`): Force the perimeter force player into an instantaneous declare so the pitch punishes any aggressive trigger.. Key conflict: Field Corner (force player). Tell cue: The quarterback never rides a mesh before arcing — every other pistol run seats the ball for at least a full step.

### Art Briles' Baylor Vertical Choice Spread (`baylor-choice`) — Era: `past-college`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Art Briles (Baylor Bears (2008-15))
- **Philosophy**: The Baylor vertical choice spread weaponized run action into touchdown shots. Every call starts with an inside-zone read, jet sweep, or screen picture that forces the second level to defend the box, then punishes whichever safety leans with single-word choice routes and doubled posts over the top. Defenses had to guard the entire deep field on every snap or concede six.
- **Plays**:
  - [Slot Choice Shot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-slot-choice-shot) (`baylor-slot-choice-shot`): Use simple inside-zone action to freeze the second level while the slot runs a leverage-based vertical shot for a touchdown.. Key conflict: Nickel (run-fit defender on the slot). Tell cue: The slot releases instantly vertical with no stem variation — a true option route adjusts mid-route; this one never breaks.
  - [IZ Read + Choice Double-Post](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-iz-read-choice-double-post) (`baylor-iz-read-choice-double-post`): Pair a true zone-read pull with a double-post shot so the run action buys the second level while the safety is forced to defend both deep middles alone.. Key conflict: Free safety (single-high, caught between two posts). Tell cue: The ball stays in the quarterback's hands after the mesh — a pure zone-read RPO would throw immediately off the read instead of pulling and climbing to set feet.
  - [Bubble-Go Glance](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-bubble-go-glance) (`baylor-bubble-go-glance`): Sell the bubble-screen picture to trigger the force defenders uphill, then convert the slot to a glance vertical that attacks the vacated seam.. Key conflict: Nickel (the screen trigger). Tell cue: The slot's first two steps carry him toward the sideline like a true bubble — but a real bubble keeps flattening; this one plants and climbs at the numbers.
  - [Speed Sweep Constraint](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-speed-sweep-constraint) (`baylor-speed-sweep-constraint`): Force both perimeter defenders to defend the sideline honestly so they cannot cheat toward the choice shots this family lives on.. Key conflict: Nickel (the force player). Tell cue: The ball changes hands to a full-speed receiver crossing the formation — no other call in this family puts the ball on the perimeter before the second level moves.

### Urban Meyer's Spread Option (`meyer-spread-option`) — Era: `past-college`
- **Architect / Head Coach**: Urban Meyer (Florida / Ohio State (2001-18))
- **Philosophy**: The Meyer spread option pairs zone-read runs and inverted veer with snag-triangle passing, all built on one principle: make the defense defend the quarterback as a runner on every snap. Perimeter jet motion and reverse constraints stretch the field horizontally while the read game attacks it vertically. Two national championships were built on this foundation.
- **Plays**:
  - [Inside Zone Read Give](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-inside-zone-read-give) (`meyer-inside-zone-read-give`): Make the backside end choose between the quarterback and the A-gap, then punish the crash with an instant downhill give.. Key conflict: Backside Defensive End (unblocked read key). Tell cue: The ball leaves the quarterback's hands before his shoulders ever turn — a true keep rides through the mesh point.
  - [Inverted Veer Power Read](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-inverted-veer-power-read) (`meyer-inverted-veer-power-read`): Use a jet sweep presentation to displace the playside end, then attack the vacated interior with a quarterback pull.. Key conflict: Playside Defensive End (unblocked read key). Tell cue: The ballcarrier crosses the formation before the mesh ever happens — classic zone reads have no motion at the snap.
  - [Snag Triangle Spacing](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-snag-triangle-spacing) (`meyer-snag-triangle-spacing`): Attack Cover 3 with three-layer spacing that puts every single defender in an impossible high-low conflict.. Key conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong curl-flat defender). Tell cue: The running back releases to the flat instead of carrying a dive fake — live read-option plays never send the back away from the mesh.
  - [Speed Option w/ Reverse Constraint](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-speed-option-reverse) (`meyer-speed-option-reverse`): Attack the perimeter with a speed option while a reverse-constraint motion freezes the backside from pursuing.. Key conflict: Field Corner (force player). Tell cue: Motion moves away from the run direction at full sprint — normal speed-option motions always move toward the play.

## Defensive Scheme Families (20 Systems / 80 Plays)

### Robert Saleh's 4-3 Wide-9 & Cover 3 Match (`saleh-43-wide9`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Robert Saleh (San Francisco 49ers / NY Jets)
- **Philosophy**: A masterclass in modern defensive front geometry and disciplined coverage matching. Built around aggressive Wide-9 defensive end splits and penetrating 3-techniques that generate elite 4-man pressure, complemented by pattern-matching Cover 3 Rip/Liz, split-field Cover 6 brackets, and timed A-gap cross-dog blitzes.
- **Plays**:
  - [Cover 3 Match (Rip/Liz)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=saleh-43-wide9&play=saleh-cover3-match) (`saleh-cover3-match`): Generate organic 4-man pass rush via Wide-9 speed angles while suffocating passing concepts with pattern-matching Cover 3 Rip/Liz rules.. Key conflict: WDE (Wide-9 speed rusher) & SAM (Apex match defender on slot seam). Tell cue: Base single-high alignment with SS rolling into the 8-man box/overhang at snap
  - [Cover 6 Split-Field Bracket](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=saleh-43-wide9&play=saleh-cover6-bracket) (`saleh-cover6-bracket`): Counter 3x1 Trips formations and flood concepts that typically stress single-high Cover 3 by deploying split-field Quarters to the field and Cover 2 to the boundary.. Key conflict: RCB (Field Corner) & SS (Field Safety) in Quarters bracket technique. Tell cue: Field safety stays deep in Quarters alignment instead of buzzing down into the box at snap
  - [4-3 Cross-Dog Fire Zone 3](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=saleh-43-wide9&play=saleh-cross-dog-fire3) (`saleh-cross-dog-fire3`): Manufacture guaranteed interior penetration against standard 5-man/6-man slide pass protections using a synchronized A-gap cross-dog blitz.. Key conflict: WILL (Delayed A-gap blitzer) & MIKE (Point-of-attack pick blitzer). Tell cue: Mike & Will sprint downhill at snap to cross interior gaps instead of reading backfield run flow
  - [NASCAR Package Cover 1 Robber](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=saleh-43-wide9&play=saleh-nascar-cover1-robber) (`saleh-nascar-cover1-robber`): Deploy maximum pass rush speed (4 defensive ends) on 3rd-and-long while setting a Cover 1 Robber trap to jump intermediate crossing and dig routes.. Key conflict: SS (Robber / Lurk defender) & WDE (Speed edge rusher). Tell cue: Pass-rush front widens into NASCAR splits and SS drops to low robber hole rather than deep 1/3

### Mike Macdonald's Hybrid Disguise & Sim Pressures (`macdonald-hybrid-disguise`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Mike Macdonald (Baltimore Ravens / Seattle Seahawks)
- **Philosophy**: The cutting edge of NFL defensive design. Built on pre-snap ambiguity, Amoeba and Double-A mug presentations, 4-man simulated pressures (Creepers) that drop interior linemen into passing windows, post-snap safety spins into corner traps, and lethal 6-man Cover 0 peel blitzes that force quarterbacks into impossible post-snap calculations.
- **Plays**:
  - [Double-A Mug to Cover 3 Buzz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=macdonald-hybrid-disguise&play=macdonald-double-mug-buzz) (`macdonald-double-mug-buzz`): Manufacture pre-snap protection chaos and force inaccurate hot throws by showing a 6-man Cover 0 blitz, then dropping 7 defenders into a suffocating Cover 3 Buzz shell.. Key conflict: WILL (A-gap bail linebacker) & SS (Downhill Buzz safety). Tell cue: Base mug look where both mugged linebackers bail into hook zones at snap while SS buzzes down
  - [4-Man Creeper Fire Zone (Sim Blitz)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=macdonald-hybrid-disguise&play=macdonald-creeper-overload) (`macdonald-creeper-overload`): Manufacture an unblocked free rusher (Nickel DB) while keeping 7 coverage defenders on the field by dropping interior DT into the quick hot-throw window.. Key conflict: NICKEL (Unblocked creeper blitzer) & 3T (Interior simulated dropper). Tell cue: Nickel DB triggers on a blitz trajectory while 3-Tech drops into the shallow throwing lane
  - [Single-High to Cover 6 Trap](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=macdonald-hybrid-disguise&play=macdonald-split-field-trap) (`macdonald-split-field-trap`): Bait opposing quarterbacks into throwing standard Cover 3 beaters (out routes and sail concepts) by feigning a single-high middle-of-field-closed shell before spinning into a deadly Cover 6 corner trap.. Key conflict: LCB (Trap Corner) & SS (Disguised deep half safety). Tell cue: Free safety spins from middle-of-field-closed to deep half post-snap, triggering corner trap
  - [Amoeba Overload House Blitz (Cover 0 Peel)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=macdonald-hybrid-disguise&play=macdonald-amoeba-cover0-peel) (`macdonald-amoeba-cover0-peel`): Deploy maximum chaos and bring a 6-man overload house blitz on money downs, using the Peel technique on the edge to eliminate the QB’s hot checkdown.. Key conflict: WDE (Peel defender on RB) & MIKE (Unblocked interior blitzer). Tell cue: All mugged rushers explode forward with no underneath droppers, edge peeling on RB

### Brian Flores' Psycho Front & Cover 0 Pressure (`belichick-flores-psycho`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Brian Flores (Minnesota Vikings / New England Patriots)
- **Philosophy**: An extreme binary pressure system rooted in Bill Belichick chameleon football and weaponized by Brian Flores into the NFL’s most terrifying pre-snap presentation. By crowding the line of scrimmage with 6 to 7 mugged rushers in the Psycho Front, the defense creates identical pre-snap chaos before either sending an unblockable 7-man Cover 0 house blitz, bluffing and dropping 8 into muddy coverage traps, executing interior A-gap cross-dog twists, or bracketing the offense’s #1 star wide receiver.
- **Plays**:
  - [Psycho 7-Man All-Out House Blitz (Cover 0)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-flores-psycho&play=cover0-all-out-house) (`cover0-all-out-house`): Overwhelm 5-man and 6-man pass protections with an unblockable 7-man zero-safety house blitz, forcing an immediate sub-2.0s throw or violent sack.. Key conflict: LURKER (Unblocked interior house rusher) & LCB (Zero-safety press lock). Tell cue: All 7 defenders at the line of scrimmage rush full-tilt, leaving cornerbacks in pure zero-safety press man.
  - [Psycho Bluff Drop-8 Lurk](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-flores-psycho&play=drop8-psycho-lurk) (`drop8-psycho-lurk`): Exploit the quarterback’s conditioned fear of the Cover 0 house blitz by bluffing 7 rushers and bailing 4 into the exact hot throwing windows.. Key conflict: LURKER (Floating middle robber/lurker). Tell cue: Four mugged rushers bail backward at snap into intermediate zone cushions while 3 rushers push pocket.
  - [Psycho 6-Man Cross-Dog Fire Hot](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-flores-psycho&play=cross-dog-fire-hot) (`cross-dog-fire-hot`): Defeat slide protections and 6-man half-slide schemes by manufacturing instant interior penetration via an A-gap cross-dog twist while protecting the deep field with Hot coverage.. Key conflict: LB_A2 (Looping A-gap crosser) & LB_A1 (Penetrating pick rusher). Tell cue: Inside linebackers cross through opposite A-gaps on a delayed twist stunt behind edge contain.
  - [Psycho Chameleon Bracket (Double #1 Star)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-flores-psycho&play=bracket-doubles-star) (`bracket-doubles-star`): Eliminate the opponent’s primary star wide receiver using a Belichick-style bracket double-team disguised out of Flores’ signature 7-man psycho mug front.. Key conflict: LCB & LURKER (Bracket tandem on #1 Star WR). Tell cue: Boundary corner plays outside leverage while safety brackets inside hip of star receiver in high-low double.

### Vic Fangio's Two-High Shell & Quarters Matching (`fangio-two-high-shell`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Vic Fangio (Philadelphia Eagles / Denver Broncos)
- **Philosophy**: The defensive philosophy that reshaped modern NFL game-planning. Built on a static, impenetrable two-high safety shell pre-snap that disguises split-field Cover 6 (Quarter-Quarter-Half), Palms Match Quarters (2-Read), Drop-8 simulated creeper pressures, and lethal boundary corner traps. Paired with light-box 5-1-5 Penny fronts that suffocate explosive passing concepts while matching underneath crossing routes.
- **Plays**:
  - [Cover 6 (Quarter-Quarter-Half Split Safety)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=fangio-two-high-shell&play=cover6-quarter-quarter-half) (`cover6-quarter-quarter-half`): Present an ambiguous 2-high shell pre-snap, then split the field into Quarters to the passing strength and Cover 2 to the boundary to suffocate vertical seams and intermediate outs.. Key conflict: Field Safety (FS) matching #2 seam and Boundary CB (LCB) playing cloud squat on the flat. Tell cue: Base split-safety structure: Field safety matches slot seam in Quarters while Boundary safety rolls to deep half.
  - [Penny 5-1-5 Match Quarters (Palms / 2-Read)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=fangio-two-high-shell&play=penny-match-quarters) (`penny-match-quarters`): Deploy symmetrical 4-deep match (Palms / 2-Read) from the identical 2-high pre-snap shell to jump quick out routes and rob crossing patterns.. Key conflict: STAR (Nickel) reading #2 out-break and BS (Boundary Safety) driving top-down on #1. Tell cue: Both safeties trigger top-down at 10-12 yards matching #2 receivers vertical while Star DB plays palms flat.
  - [Tite Creeper Drop-8 Coverage Trap](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=fangio-two-high-shell&play=tite-creeper-drop8) (`tite-creeper-drop8`): Simulate a heavy 5-man Penny rush pre-snap, then drop both outside linebackers into underneath passing lanes to eliminate quick-game hot reads in Drop-8 coverage.. Key conflict: LOLB & ROLB executing bluff-and-drop into hook-curl passing lanes. Tell cue: Both edge rushers bluff penetration then bail into intermediate hook-curl lanes as defense drops 8.
  - [Cover 8 Boundary Corner Trap](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=fangio-two-high-shell&play=cover8-boundary-trap) (`cover8-boundary-trap`): Bait the quarterback into throwing a boundary intermediate out-route against what appears to be soft Quarters cushion, only for the boundary corner to trap the route while the safety caps deep.. Key conflict: LCB (Boundary Corner) timing the trap break and BS (Boundary Safety) capping deep vertical routes. Tell cue: Boundary corner squats and traps out-route underneath while Boundary safety rotates over top.

### Jesse Minter's Amoeba Front & Simulated Creepers (`minter-amoeba-creeper`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Jesse Minter (Baltimore Ravens / Los Angeles Chargers)
- **Philosophy**: A masterclass in pre-snap psychological warfare and simulated pressure architectures. Jesse Minter combines standing 6-up Amoeba fronts, slot corner simulated blitzes (Creepers) dropping athletic defensive ends, disguised Cover 1 Lurk rotations that bait quarterbacks into underneath robber traps, and lethal Double-A mug Cover 0 peel blitzes that neutralize hot reads.
- **Plays**:
  - [Amoeba Front 5-Man Fire Zone 3](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=minter-amoeba-creeper&play=minter-amoeba-fire-zone3) (`minter-amoeba-fire-zone3`): Use pre-snap Amoeba chaos to dictate offensive pass protections, then bring a timed 5-man A-gap fire pressure while dropping the mugged MIKE directly into the hot slant lane.. Key conflict: WILL (weak A-gap blitzer) & MIKE (Amoeba bail linebacker). Tell cue: Standing 6-up look where 5 rushers fire while MIKE bails to strong hook and SS buzzes down to boundary flat
  - [Nickel Slot Blitz Creeper (Simulated Pressure)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=minter-amoeba-creeper&play=minter-slot-blitz-creeper) (`minter-slot-blitz-creeper`): Manufacture free edge pressure with only a 4-man rush by dropping a defensive end into coverage while sending a lightning-fast slot defensive back.. Key conflict: NICKEL (unblocked slot blitzer) & WDE (creeper flat dropper). Tell cue: Standard 4-down look where SDE spikes inside to pin the RT while Nickel blitzes from the slot and WDE drops into coverage
  - [Amoeba Cover 1 Robber Lurk](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=minter-amoeba-creeper&play=minter-cover1-robber-lurk) (`minter-cover1-robber-lurk`): Show all-out blitz pre-snap to force quick man-beating throws (Mesh/Slants), then drop a linebacker into the low hole to bait and intercept the quarterback.. Key conflict: MIKE (Lurk / Rat-in-the-hole robber linebacker). Tell cue: Pre-snap sugar front rotates into Cover 1 Man-Free with MIKE squatting as a middle-hole robber on crossers
  - [Double-A Mug Cover 0 Peel Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=minter-amoeba-creeper&play=minter-double-mug-peel) (`minter-double-mug-peel`): Create instant interior pressure with a Double-A gap blitz while utilizing a "peel" technique to automatically erase the offense’s built-in hot check to the running back.. Key conflict: WILL (A-gap mug blitzer with peel responsibility) & MIKE (interior blitzer). Tell cue: Both A-gap linebackers mug pre-snap, with WILL peeling to cover the flaring RB while MIKE rushes the A-gap and corners play press man

### DeMeco Ryans' Wide-9 Attack & Match Coverage (`ryans-wide9-attack`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: DeMeco Ryans (Houston Texans)
- **Philosophy**: An aggressive, downhill defensive system engineered around pure physical dominance and geometric leverage. Features extreme Wide-9 defensive end alignments and Tackle-Wrap stunt games that crush pass protections with 4 rushers, backed by split-field Cover 2 Palms (2-Read) cloud traps, Cover 1 Low-Hole mug looks, and field-overload 5-man fire zones.
- **Plays**:
  - [Wide-9 Under Front Tackle-Wrap Stunt (T-E)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=ryans-wide9-attack&play=ryans-wide9-under-tackle-wrap) (`ryans-wide9-under-tackle-wrap`): Exploit the Wide-9 alignment by forcing offensive tackles into elongated kick-slides, then executing a Tackle-End (T-E) wrap stunt to create an unblocked interior rush lane for the defensive end.. Key conflict: SDE (looping edge rusher) & 3T (interior spike tackle). Tell cue: Wide-9 DE takes an exaggerated outside step before looping sharply inside behind the interior 3-technique spike
  - [Split-Safety Palms (2-Read) Match](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=ryans-wide9-attack&play=ryans-cover2-palms-read) (`ryans-cover2-palms-read`): Obliterate standard Smash and quick-out concepts by using split-field 2-Read (Palms) matching, enabling the cornerback to trap underneath out routes while the safety caps deep corner routes.. Key conflict: LCB (Palms flat trap corner) & SS (over-the-top corner cap safety). Tell cue: Two-high shell where the cornerback reads the #2 slot receiver and aggressively jumps the out-route while safety carries #1 deep
  - [Cover 1 Hole with Linebacker A-Gap Mug](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=ryans-wide9-attack&play=ryans-cover1-hole-mug) (`ryans-cover1-hole-mug`): Threaten A-gap pressure to force quick slant/in routes, then drop the mugged linebacker into the low hole to bracket underneath passes while the 4-man Wide-9 front collapses the pocket.. Key conflict: MIKE (A-gap mug low-hole robber) & 3T (interior penetrator). Tell cue: MIKE mugs the A-gap pre-snap then immediately drops 5 yards into the low hole while corners press and safeties roll into single-high robber
