  - [5-Man Overload Edge Fire Zone](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=ryans-wide9-attack&play=ryans-overload-edge-fire) (`ryans-overload-edge-fire`): Overload the field side of the pass protection with a 5-man fire zone blitz, creating an unblocked perimeter rusher while dropping the boundary defensive end into coverage.. Key conflict: NICKEL (unblocked overload blitzer) & WDE (boundary flat dropper). Tell cue: Field-side overload pressure with SDE slanting inside to clear the edge for Nickel DB while boundary DE drops into coverage

### Chris Shula's Match Quarters & Penny Front Shell (`shula-match-quarters`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Chris Shula (Los Angeles Rams)
- **Philosophy**: A Fangio-lineage two-high quarters system refined for the modern spread era. Chris Shula employs light Tite (4i-0-4i) and Penny (5-1-5) fronts to maintain interior gap integrity with fewer bodies in the box, while presenting a perpetual two-safety shell that disguises Cover 6, Cover 8, and split-field quarters match calls. Creeper blitzes — defenders who simulate pressure but drop into coverage — are the signature deception weapon that renders pre-snap hot-read systems unreliable.
- **Plays**:
  - [Tite Front B-Gap Pinch with Match Quarters](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-tite-b-gap-pinch) (`shula-tite-b-gap-pinch`): Suffocate inside zone and Duo run concepts with a 3-man Tite front (404 alignment) by pinching the B-gaps, spilling the ball carrier into the waiting arms of unblocked edge defenders and downhill safeties.. Key conflict: 4iL (B-gap pinch tackle) & BS (downhill alley-fitting boundary safety). Tell cue: 3-4 Tite front where both 4i interior linemen slant hard into the B-gaps spilling run action to perimeter OLBs and downhill safeties
  - [Penny 5-1-5 Bracket Coverage vs Condensed Bunch](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-penny-bracket-bunch) (`shula-penny-bracket-bunch`): Eliminate natural pick and rub routes from condensed bunch sets by employing a 3-over-2 Triangle Bracket match coverage while retaining a disciplined 4-man Penny rush.. Key conflict: STAR (inside bracket DB) & FS (top cap safety). Tell cue: Penny 5-1-5 front with STAR, corner, and safety forming a tight triangle bracket over the condensed bunch to exchange routes in-and-out
  - [Split-Field Cover 8 (Quarter-Quarter-Half)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-cover8-field-quarter) (`shula-cover8-field-quarter`): Exploit tendencies against two-high shells by splitting the field coverage: playing Quarters match to the multi-receiver field side and a hard Cover 2 trap to the boundary to intercept quick out-routes.. Key conflict: LCB (Boundary trap corner) & BS (Boundary deep half safety). Tell cue: Two-high pre-snap shell where boundary corner squats in hard flat while boundary safety rolls over top into deep half
  - [Boundary Creeper with Drop-7 Quarter Coverage Shell](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-boundary-creeper-drop7) (`shula-boundary-creeper-drop7`): Drop 7 defenders into multi-layered zone coverage by disguising a pass rusher as a creeper, then rushing only 3 linemen while flooding all throwing windows.. Key conflict: Left OLB Creeper (Pre-snap Rush Alignment, Post-snap Drop). Tell cue: LOLB walks up to line in edge rush stance before snap — this is the creeper tell; if he drops, expect a 3-man rush with 7 in coverage.

### Steve Spagnuolo Exotic Blitz & Sim Pressures (`spagnuolo-exotic-blitz`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Steve Spagnuolo (Kansas City Chiefs)
- **Philosophy**: Steve Spagnuolo’s championship-winning defensive scheme: aggressive situational blitzing, boundary corner overloads, 4-man creeper simulated pressures dropping interior linemen, 7-man Cover 0 house heat, and disguised inverted split-safety coverages that break standard quarterback protection reads.
- **Plays**:
  - [Boundary Corner Blitz (Spags Heat)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-corndog-corner-blitz) (`spagnuolo-corndog-corner-blitz`): Manufacture an unblockable blindside corner blitz by manipulating offensive protection with an interior DE stunt while rotating the free safety into the vacated flat.. Key conflict: LCB (Boundary Corner Blitz) & FS (Flat Replacement Safety). Tell cue: LCB shows press alignment with no safety help over the top, then sprints downhill at snap while FS rotates down
  - [Cross-Dog Creeper Sim Pressure](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-cross-creeper-drop) (`spagnuolo-cross-creeper-drop`): Generate unblocked pressure with a 4-man simulated rush by replacing a dropping defensive end with a blitzing linebacker into the offense’s slide protection.. Key conflict: WILL (Creeper Linebacker Rusher) & WDE (Dropping Defensive End). Tell cue: Defensive end steps back into hook drop at snap while off-ball linebacker triggers forward into B-gap
  - [Cover 0 Max All-Out Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-cover0-max-heat) (`spagnuolo-cover0-max-heat`): Overwhelm 5- and 6-man pass protections on critical 3rd & long downs by sending 7 rushers while playing tight press-man coverage without safety help.. Key conflict: SS (Unblocked 7th Edge Rusher) & FS (Press-Man DB on Slot H). Tell cue: All 7 front defenders rush at snap with DBs pressing at 1 yard depth and no safety retreating deep
  - [Split-Safety Invert Cover 2 Trap](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-split-safety-invert2) (`spagnuolo-split-safety-invert2`): Deceive the quarterback by disguising a two-deep shell as single-high, inverting cornerbacks into deep halves while safeties trigger downhill to trap intermediate seams and out routes.. Key conflict: FS (Downhill Invert Safety) & LCB (Deep-Half Sinking Corner). Tell cue: Corners sprint backwards into deep halves at snap while both safeties drive downhill into underneath curl/flat zones

### Dan Quinn Cover 3 Press-Bail & Under Front (`quinn-cover3-press`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Dan Quinn (Washington Commanders / Seattle Seahawks)
- **Philosophy**: Dan Quinn’s definitive single-high defensive system: physical press-bail cornerback mechanics, 4-3 Under front overloads generating organic 4-man speed rush with the LEO defensive end, Cover 1 Rat-in-the-Hole lurking underneath crossers, and lethal safety Sky fire zone pressures.
- **Plays**:
  - [Cover 3 Press-Bail (Legion Foundation)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=quinn-cover3-press&play=quinn-cover3-press-bail) (`quinn-cover3-press-bail`): Suffocate explosive perimeter passing using physical press-bail cornerback technique and single-high Cover 3 Sky integrity while creating speed pressure with the Wide-9 LEO rusher.. Key conflict: LCB (Press-Bail Corner) & LEO (Wide-9 Speed Edge Rusher). Tell cue: Corners show hard press at line then open hips into side-saddle bail at snap while SS rotates downhill
  - [4-3 Under Front Overload Collapse](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=quinn-cover3-press&play=quinn-under-front-overload) (`quinn-under-front-overload`): Create immediate organic pass-rush disruption using 4-3 Under front alignment angles to generate simultaneous weakside edge speed and strongside interior 3T penetration.. Key conflict: 3T (Penetrating Under DT) & LEO (Weakside Edge Rusher). Tell cue: 1-tech and 3-tech shifted into Under front alignment with LEO stretched out in Wide-9 stance
  - [Cover 1 Rat-in-the-Hole (Lurk Crosser)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=quinn-cover3-press&play=quinn-cover1-rat-in-hole) (`quinn-cover1-rat-in-hole`): Neutralize man-beating Mesh and shallow cross combinations by freeing an underneath defender (The Rat) to lurk in the short intermediate hole while corners play trail technique.. Key conflict: MIKE (Rat-in-the-Hole Lurker) & FS (Deep Post Safety). Tell cue: Middle linebacker mugs A-gap then immediately drops to 6 yards depth as a free-floating lurker while DBs play tight trail man
  - [Safety Sky Fire Zone (3-Deep 2-Under)](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=quinn-cover3-press&play=quinn-safety-sky-fire-zone) (`quinn-safety-sky-fire-zone`): Create a devastating overload edge blitz using Strong Safety from depth on a Sky path while dropping the defensive end to take away the primary hot throw.. Key conflict: SS (Blazing Sky Edge Rusher) & SDE (Dropping Flat Defender). Tell cue: Strong safety creeps towards line before snap and launches outside as SAM crashes inside on tackle

### Todd Bowles Creeper Blitz & Psycho Front (`bowles-creeper-blitz`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Todd Bowles (Tampa Bay Buccaneers)
- **Philosophy**: Todd Bowles’ fearsome defensive scheme: Dual A-gap cross-dog interior stunts, boundary corner overloads attacking pass protection slides, Drop-8 Tampa 2 traps with the middle linebacker running the deep pole, and 4-man simulated pressures with edge peel rules.
- **Plays**:
  - [Dual A-Gap Cross-Dog Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=bowles-creeper-blitz&play=bowles-dual-a-gap-cross-blitz) (`bowles-dual-a-gap-cross-blitz`): Create immediate interior pressure against slide protections by sending a two-man A-gap cross-dog stunt where the first linebacker picks the center and the second loops untouched to the quarterback.. Key conflict: WILL (Looping A-Gap Blitzer) & MIKE (Penetrating Center Picker). Tell cue: Both inside linebackers mug A-gaps at snap, with MIKE charging first and WILL crossing behind his back into opposite gap
  - [Boundary Overload Fire Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=bowles-creeper-blitz&play=bowles-overload-boundary-fire) (`bowles-overload-boundary-fire`): Exploit half-slide offensive protections toward passing strength by launching an unblockable boundary corner overload while rotating safety coverage into the vacated perimeter void.. Key conflict: LCB (Boundary Corner Blitzer) & LOLB (Pinning Defensive End). Tell cue: Boundary corner creeps close to line with inside tilt while safety aligns at 12 yards on boundary hash preparing to rotate down
  - [Drop-8 Tampa 2 Middle Lurk Trap](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=bowles-creeper-blitz&play=bowles-drop8-tampa2-lurk) (`bowles-drop8-tampa2-lurk`): Create catastrophic quarterback turnovers on long passing downs by bluffing an all-out 7-man blitz and dropping 8 defenders into a suffocating Tampa 2 shell with the middle linebacker running the pole.. Key conflict: MIKE (Deep Middle Pole Runner) & WILL (Intermediate Hook Dropper). Tell cue: 7-man front shows all-out heat, then 4 line-of-scrimmage defenders turn their backs and sprint into coverage zones at the snap
  - [Peel-Zone Simulated Pressure](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=bowles-creeper-blitz&play=bowles-peel-zone-sim-pressure) (`bowles-peel-zone-sim-pressure`): Manufacture an unblocked 4-man simulated pressure from the slot while utilizing peel rules on the edge defender to eliminate the offense’s primary hot checkdown to the running back.. Key conflict: LOLB (Peel Technique Edge Dropper) & NCB (Sim Creeper Blitzer). Tell cue: Edge rusher turns outside immediately to match running back release while slot cornerback sprints downhill on blindside track

### Buddy Ryan's 46 Defense (`buddy-46-defense`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Buddy Ryan (Chicago Bears (1982-85))
- **Philosophy**: The most aggressive defense in NFL history. Ends aligned head-up at tight-end width, tackles shaded inside, three linebackers bunched at 2-3 yards, and BOTH safeties walked into an eight-man box with zero deep-middle help. Corners survive on islands in press-man. The base picture alone forces offenses to abandon their blocking rules; the mad-dog mug, E-X-T combo, and free blade blitzes turn that confusion into sacks.
- **Plays**:
  - [Base 46 vs Pro I-Form](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-base-i-form) (`b46-base-i-form`): Commit nine defenders to the box with walked safeties and bunched linebackers so any base run is met at or behind the line of scrimmage with a blocker-free defender.. Key conflict: SS at 5 yards — the extra force player who turns every one-gap run into a two-hat fit. Tell cue: Both safeties aligned INSIDE the tackles at 5 and 8 yards — the pure 46 picture has no safety deeper than the linebackers’ original depth.
  - [Double A-Gap Mad Dog Overload](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-mad-dog-double-a) (`b46-mad-dog-double-a`): Overload both A-gaps with walked defenders so the offense’s pass-protection slide cannot account for every interior threat, forcing an instant-pressure throw or sack.. Key conflict: SS mugged over the strong A-gap — the blocker assigned to him cannot get depth fast enough. Tell cue: Both A-gap defenders are standing upright at 1.2 yards staring across the line pre-snap — the base 46 keeps its safeties at 5 and 8 yards instead.
  - [Strong-Side E-X-T Combo Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-ext-strong-combo) (`b46-ext-strong-combo`): Send three staggered strong-side rushers (end-B gap, tackle-C loop, linebacker-edge) so one protection slide always leaves the second-wave looper unblocked.. Key conflict: DT running the loop — his path is invisible until he bursts out of the crashing end’s trash. Tell cue: The shaded tackle swings wide behind the crashing end rather than firing straight — pure interior slants never leave the box.
  - [Weak Free Blade Safety Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-free-blade-weak-blitz) (`b46-free-blade-weak-blitz`): Trade the free safety for a free weak-side runner while the boundary corner replaces him deep, keeping single-high shell integrity behind a five-man pressure.. Key conflict: FS on the blade — unblocked by design because MIKE’s strong-side walk-up steals the running back’s scan. Tell cue: One safety at 8 yards directly over the weak guard with a corner pressed opposite — the base 46 keeps both safeties in the box and no corner ever bails from the middle of the field.

### Dick LeBeau's Zone Blitz Fire Zone Family (`lebeau-fire-zone`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Dick LeBeau (Pittsburgh Steelers (1995-2014))
- **Philosophy**: The definitive zone-blitz system: true 5-man pressures where a defensive lineman or safety trades his rush lane for a rat/hook zone while replacement blitzers attack vacated gaps. Every call pairs 3-deep/3-under fire zone coverage behind disguised rotations from Cover 2 and single-high shells, forcing hot answers directly into dropped rushers.
- **Plays**:
  - [Triple Inside Fire Zone](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-triple-inside-fire) (`fz-triple-inside-fire`): Generate true 5-man pressure with a double-A linebacker blast while a defensive end secretly trades his rush lane for the rat zone that swallows hot answers.. Key conflict: RDE executing the rat trade drop. Tell cue: The strong end loosens his stance and takes a lateral first step rather than an upfield punch, signaling the trade before the ball is even thrown.
  - [Safety Rotate Fire Zone](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-safety-rotate-fire) (`fz-safety-rotate-fire`): Show a static Cover 2 shell to bait quick-game answers, then rotate to single-high Cover 3 fire zone coverage behind five-man pressure.. Key conflict: Strong safety executing the downhill rotation. Tell cue: Both safeties start at equal nine-yard depths like true Cover 2 halves; the tell is the strong safety leaning forward in his pedal at the snap instead of backpedaling.
  - [Nose Drop Nasco](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-nose-drop-nasco) (`fz-nose-drop-nasco`): Bait a run-first protection with a light odd front, exchange the nose for an A-gap blitzing linebacker plus two inside-slanting OLBs, and cover the deep middle with the dropped nose himself.. Key conflict: Nose tackle executing the nasco middle-hook drop. Tell cue: The zero-tech nose takes a lateral first step away from the Center rather than a contact punch, revealing the drop before the mesh is sold.
  - [Safety Blitz Smoke](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-safety-blitz-smoke) (`fz-safety-blitz-smoke`): Force an instant throw with a disguised safety blitz while the corner manufactures and then steals the curl window the QB is trained to trust.. Key conflict: Boundary corner executing the curl-bait jump. Tell cue: Both safeties align deep like shell coverage, but the strong safety has his inside foot back and eyes locked on the guard-center tandem instead of the receivers.

### Tony Dungy's Tampa 2 (`tampa-2`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Tony Dungy (Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1996-2001))
- **Philosophy**: The defining middle-of-field-closed Cover 2 of its era: a penetrating four-man rush behind corners who squat in the deep halves with underneath-first eyes, and safeties splitting the field. The signature wrinkle is the Mike linebacker converting his hook-curl drop into a full sprint to the deep-middle hole, erasing the seams that normally kill Cover 2. Quick perimeter answers are contested instantly, forcing quarterbacks to hold for seam throws that sail straight into the sprinting Mike.
- **Plays**:
  - [Base Tampa 2 vs 2x2](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=tampa-2&play=t2-base-vs-2x2) (`t2-base-vs-2x2`): Flood the deep zones with five defenders while rushing only four, baiting offenses into the seams and erasing them with the Mike linebacker’s unique deep-middle conversion.. Key conflict: MIKE turning his hook-curl drop into the deep-middle hole — the only defender who can erase both seams. Tell cue: Both corners squat at 10 yards staring at the QB instead of trailing receivers vertically — cloud keeps its boundary corner pressed at 1 yard.
  - [SLB Edge Blitz Variant](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=tampa-2&play=t2-slb-edge-blitz) (`t2-slb-edge-blitz`): Add a fifth rusher off the edge without weakening the Tampa 2 structure by having the Will exchange directly into the Sam’s vacated hook-curl window.. Key conflict: SAM off the edge — the tight end must take the inside LE, leaving the rim completely bare. Tell cue: The Sam linebacker stands upright at 4 yards staring at the tackle’s outside shoulder — the base Tampa 2 keeps him stacked over the tight end at 4.5.
  - [Cover 2 Roll to Cover 3 Sky vs Trips](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=tampa-2&play=t2-roll-cover3-trips) (`t2-roll-cover3-trips`): Answer a trips overload by rotating out of the baited two-high shell into three-deep coverage, trading one deep half for a middle-third eraser without weakening the flood side.. Key conflict: FS spinning from his weak half to the deep middle third — the rotation that turns a flood beater into a contested throw. Tell cue: The free safety starts drifting toward the hash mid-cadence while the strong safety tilts flat-side — base Tampa 2 keeps both safeties perfectly still until the snap.
  - [Cloud Boundary Call](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=tampa-2&play=t2-cloud-boundary) (`t2-cloud-boundary`): Bait the boundary rhythm throw by disguising which defender owns the deep half, then exchange roles at the snap so the hot answer lands in coverage.. Key conflict: SS flashing down from his disguised half alignment — he is the one waiting in the flat the QB was promised. Tell cue: The boundary corner lines up at 7 yards instead of the base call’s 10-yard squat — base Tampa 2 never gives its corner that much cushion to the slot side.

### Tom Landry's Flex Defense (`landry-flex`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Tom Landry (Dallas Cowboys (1960-88))
- **Philosophy**: The original positional-defense blueprint that ran in Dallas for three decades. Both tackles align one yard off the ball in a staggered flex, trading penetration for patient gap-zone occupation: linemen hold their lanes, linebackers shift strength with motion, and a guaranteed three-defender convergence swallows every point of attack before it develops.
- **Plays**:
  - [Standard Weak-Tackle Flex vs Power Sweep](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-weak-tackle-power-sweep) (`flex-weak-tackle-power-sweep`): Use the one-yard flex alignment to occupy blockers passively while three defenders converge independently on the sweep point of attack without needing a blocked lane.. Key conflict: The flexed weak-side tackle on his free lateral chase. Tell cue: The weak-side tackle aligns a visible yard off the line of scrimmage with hands free, unlike his strong-side partner who stays shaded on the snap.
  - [Tackle-Tackle Flex vs Two-Back](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-tackle-tackle-two-back) (`flex-tackle-tackle-two-back`): Occupy both interior gaps passively with flexed tackles who split double teams without needing to win, funneling two-back power into a patient three-defender kill zone.. Key conflict: The flexed strong tackle executing the patient shed. Tell cue: Both defensive tackles hover a full yard off the ball with hands free pre-snap, unlike any standard shaded or nose alignment in the same front.
  - [Linebacker Strength Shift vs Motion](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-lb-strength-shift-motion) (`flex-lb-strength-shift-motion`): Answer offensive formation-strength motion with a synchronized linebacker shift so the defense is never caught flowing cross-eyed into a perimeter run.. Key conflict: The Mike linebacker executing the strength shift. Tell cue: The Mike takes visible sprint steps parallel to the line during the motion rather than shuffling, showing the shift is coached as a sprint-to-landmark rule.
  - [Flex Line Game Pass Rush](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-line-game-rush) (`flex-line-game-rush`): Manufacture a free-edge rusher without blitzing by running a staggered slant-and-wrap line game out of the flexed tackle alignments.. Key conflict: The strong tackle executing the slant-and-wrap. Tell cue: The strong tackle widens his stance and leans inward during the cadence rather than firing straight ahead, betraying the slant half of the game.

### Bum Phillips' Two-Gap 3-4 (`phillips-two-gap-34`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Bum Phillips (Houston Oilers (1975-80))
- **Philosophy**: The original two-gap 3-4 that Bum Phillips brought to the Houston Oilers: a zero-tech nose and twin 5-tech ends who ENGAGE and hold two gaps apiece rather than penetrate, occupying all five blockers so both inside linebackers can flow untouched over the tops of engaged bodies. The stand-up outside linebacker duo serves as the front's rush weapons — walking wide on passing downs, stemming across tackles' faces, and attacking rims the anchored interior keeps bare.
- **Plays**:
  - [Base Two-Gap Fits vs 21 Personnel](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-base-two-gap-fits) (`b34-base-two-gap-fits`): Trade penetration for total gap ownership — let linemen engage and control two gaps each so linebackers can run free over the top to every ball carrier.. Key conflict: RILB scraping over the top — he arrives as the unblocked tackler precisely because the line ate every block. Tell cue: All three linemen stand square reading blockers instead of charging gaps — slant fronts explode sideways off this exact patient stance.
  - [Dual Edge Rush w/ Interior Anchor](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-dual-edge-interior-anchor) (`b34-dual-edge-interior-anchor`): Weaponize the two-gap front in reverse — let the immovable interior eat every blocker while both stand-up edges attack the rim from clean angles.. Key conflict: ROLB bending inside under the tight-end hinge — the blocker braces outward for a speed rush that never comes straight. Tell cue: Both stand-up backers walk to 2 yards in sprinter stances while the interior sits patient and squared — base fits keep backers stacked behind the line at 4 yards.
  - [Stack Slant Shift](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-stack-slant-shift) (`b34-stack-slant-shift`): Disguise instant penetration inside a patient two-gap stance, then send all three linemen across blockers’ faces at once so every combo chases while linebackers replace behind.. Key conflict: NG shooting across center into strong A — he lands exactly in the lead-blocker geometry of any strong-side run. Tell cue: The interior trio tilts and staggers its steps during the cadence before exploding inward — base two-gap fits sit flat-footed reading blocks.
  - [Wildcat Walk-Up Edge](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-wildcat-walk-up-edge) (`b34-wildcat-walk-up-edge`): Break the tackle’s pass-protection key by walking between alignments and stances across his face, then attack whichever gap his eyes abandoned last.. Key conflict: ROLB stemming across the tackle’s face — every alignment change forces a reset the rusher never has to make himself. Tell cue: The strong edge keeps switching between a two-point walk and a three-point sprinter stance across the tackle’s face — base fits park him stacked at 4 yards and leave him there.

### Jimmy Johnson's Speed 4-3 (`jj-speed-43`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Jimmy Johnson (Dallas Cowboys (1989-93) / Miami Hurricanes)
- **Philosophy**: Undersized hyper-fast linemen who fire upfield at the snap instead of reading blocks, trading two-gap size for one-gap penetration chaos that wrecks blocking rules before they form. Behind the slanting front sits man-free or single-high coverage with pressed corners on islands, so every pressured throw has nowhere soft to land. The scheme finishes plays with the Miami chase rule: relentless, assigned pursuit angles that swallow ballcarriers from sideline to sideline.
- **Plays**:
  - [Penetration Slant Loop](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=jj-speed-43&play=jj43-penetration-slant-loop) (`jj43-penetration-slant-loop`): Win with pure penetration and staggered timing: tackles slant to occupy blockers while a delayed end loops through the gap their charge creates.. Key conflict: The weak end executing the delayed loop. Tell cue: The looping end takes two visible upfield steps and visibly gathers himself before redirecting inside — pure slant teams never pull off the arc.
  - [Man-Free Will Dog](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=jj-speed-43&play=jj43-man-free-will-dog) (`jj43-man-free-will-dog`): Create guaranteed interior pressure with a single A-gap dog while man-free coverage eliminates every hot answer behind it.. Key conflict: The Will linebacker triggering the A-gap dog. Tell cue: Will lines up in a true two-point mug stance with inside foot back, cocked to fire — the loop game shows a four-point rush posture instead.
  - [Miami Chase Rule Pursuit](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=jj-speed-43&play=jj43-miami-chase-rule-pursuit) (`jj43-miami-chase-rule-pursuit`): Turn perimeter runs into short gains by having all eleven defenders execute assigned pursuit angles rather than chasing the football.. Key conflict: The strong safety filling the alley as the second hat. Tell cue: The backside end takes visibly flat steps down the line of scrimmage instead of angling upfield — the chase rule targets a spot, not the runner.
  - [Goal-Line Haley Edge Rush](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=jj-speed-43&play=jj43-goal-line-haley-edge-rush) (`jj43-goal-line-haley-edge-rush`): Commit the goal-line protection strong with an over shift and slant package, then let one isolated edge rusher decide a short-field possession.. Key conflict: The hand-down wide end rushing off the right edge. Tell cue: The strong tight end snaps down to the slanting tackle at the snap — a true goal-line run keeps him glued to the wide end instead.

### Bill Belichick's Okie/Bear Package (`belichick-okie-bear`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Bill Belichick (New England Patriots (2003-19))
- **Philosophy**: The compressed odd-front situational package Belichick deployed to bury Peyton Manning-era Colts offenses. A zero-tech nose flanked by double 4i tackles and stacked 5-tech ends gives New England five interior bodies against five interior blockers, while both inside linebackers mug over the A-gaps and the safeties crowd the box. Zero-nose geometry plus double-A mug threats stress every hot answer, bridging old goal-line fronts to modern mug-pressure packages.
- **Plays**:
  - [Goal-Line Bear vs Heavy Personnel](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-okie-bear&play=bear-goal-line-heavy) (`bear-goal-line-heavy`): Match heavy goal-line personnel with an extra interior body so every gap is two-gapped and no puller or kicker can find a clean block.. Key conflict: NOSE on the zero — he alone erases both A-gaps and frees the linebackers to play downhill. Tell cue: Five defenders within one yard of the ball with safeties at just 4.5 yards — the okie nickel look spreads its safeties wider and deeper.
  - [Third-and-1 Double-A Mug Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-okie-bear&play=bear-double-a-mug) (`bear-double-a-mug`): Guarantee zero yards on third-and-short by sending both mugged backers through the only gaps the offense must block, converting a run-stuffing front into instant pass overload.. Key conflict: WILL over the strong A-gap — the guard assigned to him cannot get square before the knife arrives. Tell cue: Both linebackers stand upright directly over the guards staring at the QB at 1.2 yards — the goal-line Bear keeps its backers at 3.4 yards in downhill run fits.
  - [Bear Slant Strong](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-okie-bear&play=bear-slant-strong) (`bear-slant-strong`): Trade gap-control patience for instant backfield penetration against gap runs, using synchronized one-gap movement so every blocker chases while the carrier runs into occupied gaps.. Key conflict: NOSE slanting to strong B — he lands exactly where the lead blocker is aiming. Tell cue: All three interior linemen tilt their stances and stagger their steps strong during the cadence — the goal-line Bear sits flat-footed until the ball is snapped.
  - [Bear-to-46 Stem Disguise](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-okie-bear&play=bear-to-46-stem-disguise) (`bear-to-46-stem-disguise`): Show a light okie shell to invite an inside-run check, then complete a cadence-length stem into a full 46 eight-man box before the ball carrier can redirect.. Key conflict: SS walking from 8.5 yards into a strong-B mug — his arrival converts a two-deep picture into nine bodies at the line. Tell cue: Both safeties are moving downhill during the cadence with backers tightening behind them — the settled goal-line Bear never moves until the snap.

### Dave Aranda's Tite Front & Peso Package (`aranda-tite-peso`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Dave Aranda (LSU DC (2016-19) / Baylor HC)
- **Philosophy**: A 4i-0-4i box that eliminates both B-gaps before the snap, forcing spread runs to bounce into walked-down hybrid defenders. Peso nickel/dime personnel blur the line between back-end and box — apex linebackers split the #2-receiver-to-tackle lines, split-field quarters pattern-matches every slot, and three-man simulated pressures occupy the quarterback’s escape lanes with defenders who were never rushing at all.
- **Plays**:
  - [Base Tite vs 11P Zone Read](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-base-zone-read) (`tite-base-zone-read`): Eliminate every interior gap with the 4i-0-4i box so a spread-run play must bounce to the perimeter, where the walked-down peso waits as the unblockable extra defender.. Key conflict: PESO nickel — the DB-LB hybrid whose walk-down turns a blocked-even run picture into a plus-one box. Tell cue: Both interior defenders aligned INSIDE the tackles (4i shades) rather than head-up or wide — the pure tite picture has no defender in either C-gap pre-snap.
  - [Tite 4 Simulated Pressure](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-sim-pressure) (`tite-sim-pressure`): Flash a five-man pressure from the tite box, rush only three, and occupy the quarterback’s scramble lane with a defensive end who replaces the blitzing Mike before dropping into the hook.. Key conflict: LE — the 4i whose fake rush converts a blocked pass-rusher into the hook-zone dropper sitting exactly where the quarterback escapes. Tell cue: Both Mike and dime mugged over the weak A-gap while neither 4i widened — the walk-up says blitz, but no edge defender moved, the signature of a three-rush sim.
  - [Quarters Apex Adjustment vs 2x2](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-quarters-apex) (`tite-quarters-apex`): Give every slot receiver both an underneath apex defender and a matching quarter safety so a two-by-two mesh concept can never isolate anyone or occupy both deep halves.. Key conflict: SS — the strong quarter whose carry rule converts the seam into a double team the moment Y goes vertical. Tell cue: Both linebackers aligned directly OVER the slots at apex depth instead of stacked in the B-gap boxes — the pure quarters-overload picture reserved for two-by-two.
  - [Bear Adjustment vs Condensed Twins](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-bear-condensed) (`tite-bear-condensed`): Answer condensed splits by tipping the tite box into a bear look, doubling every interior gap and walking hybrid defenders onto the twins so gap-scheme runs die at the line and quick game gets pressed.. Key conflict: EDGE — the head-up end whose inside slip of the kick-out turns the puller’s lead block into an empty lane for MIKE. Tell cue: Both 4is slid OUTSIDE their base shades with apexes cheated to 3.5 yards — four hats within a yard of the LOS versus three in the pure tite picture.

### Rocky Long's 3-3-5 Stack (`rlong-335-stack`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Rocky Long (San Diego State (2011-19) / New Mexico)
- **Philosophy**: Three down linemen with all three linebackers stacked directly behind them at identical depth, so no offense can read gap responsibility pre-snap. Five defensive backs play every down against any formation. The call is pressure-by-committee: slant-exchange games move all six box defenders one gap at a time, edge storms fire from both C-gaps, safeties and corners cross-dog through vacated lanes, and empty sets meet an all-out zero with straight man coverage behind.
- **Plays**:
  - [Base Stack Slant Exchange](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-slant-exchange) (`stack335-slant-exchange`): Hide every gap responsibility behind identical stacks, then move all six box defenders one gap at the snap so blockers chase a pre-snap picture that no longer exists while every gap stays owned.. Key conflict: MIKE exchanging to weak A — the stacked backer whose late fill owns the gap the slanting nose abandoned. Tell cue: All six box defenders in perfect single file — each linebacker exactly behind his lineman, a picture no four-man front can show.
  - [Double-Edge Storm Dog](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-double-edge-storm) (`stack335-double-edge-storm`): Storm both C-gaps with the stacked backers while the ends slant inward, so the protection must choose an edge while the anchoring nose erases any interior answer.. Key conflict: JACK — the weak stack backer whose outside burst arrives exactly after the tackle chases the slanting end inside. Tell cue: Pre-snap it reads like plain Cover 3 stack — no walk-ups anywhere; every rusher hid directly behind a lineman until the snap.
  - [Safety-Corner Cross-Dog Fire Zone](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-cross-dog-fire-zone) (`stack335-cross-dog-fire-zone`): Disguise a five-man fire zone behind a stacked single-high shell so spread protections commit to the wrong crosser while the safety-corner exchange manufactures interior heat.. Key conflict: RCB darting inside — the blitzer whose delayed inside path arrives after the protection has fully committed to the widened safety. Tell cue: Pre-snap it reads single-high Cover 3 with stacked backers — the tell is only the safety creeping to nine yards without any linebacker moving with him.
  - [All-Out Zero Pressure vs Empty](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-zero-empty) (`stack335-zero-empty`): Punish empty-protection math with a six-man committee so five blockers always face one extra rusher while every receiver is stranded alone in zero man coverage.. Key conflict: MIKE mugged over the A-gap — the free runner up the middle whose arrival coincides exactly with the forced throw. Tell cue: Both safeties AND a linebacker aligned at LOS-level depth against empty — pure zero has nobody deeper than seven yards except the corners.

### Marvin Lewis' Cover 2 Man-Under (`cover2-man-under`)
- **Architect / Coordinator**: Marvin Lewis (Baltimore Ravens DC (1996-2001))
- **Philosophy**: The red-zone answer of Lewis' Baltimore defenses: two safeties splitting the deep halves at full depth while five defenders play straight man underneath. Press-trail corner leverage turns every compressed release and every fade attempt into a contested footrace, with the deep halves standing as pure insurance behind the trails. When the structure needs teeth, a walked safety converts it into max pressure with one man swallowing the entire deep zone.
- **Plays**:
  - [Red-Zone 2-Man vs Compressed Twins](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-red-zone-compressed-twins) (`twoman-red-zone-compressed-twins`): Squeeze the red zone with straight man coverage under deep-half insurance so every route must beat a trail technique with no room to separate.. Key conflict: LCB playing press-trail on the compressed X — his leverage alone decides whether the beater exists. Tell cue: Both corners are pinned to their receivers at 1.5 yards while safeties sit at a full 12 — Cover 2 zone keeps its corners squatting at 10 with eyes on the QB.
  - [Fade Beater Demo](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-fade-beater-demo) (`twoman-fade-beater-demo`): Demonstrate why the classic red-zone fade fails against press-trail — the isolation throw offenses covet is exactly what this structure invites and erases.. Key conflict: LCB playing outside-leverage press — his jam converts the fade into a footrace along a sideline he already owns. Tell cue: The corner is at 1 yard with pure outside leverage staring through the receiver — soft-squat Cover 2 sits at 7 yards with eyes on the QB.
  - [2-Man Edge Blitz](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-edge-blitz) (`twoman-edge-blitz`): Convert the 2-man structure into maximum pressure by walking a safety off the edge while the lone free safety swallows the entire deep zone by himself.. Key conflict: SS blitzing off the edge — the scanning back is his only blocker and arrives a full second late. Tell cue: The strong safety stands at 2 yards beside the tight end while the free safety roams alone at 13 — base 2-man keeps both safeties splitting halves at 12.
  - [Goal-Line Double Robber](https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-goal-line-double-robber) (`twoman-goal-line-double-robber`): Protect the goal line without pressing by aligning corners over the top and converting both safeties into eye-keyed robbers who attack every throwing window in front.. Key conflict: FS as the weak-side robber — he sits on the exact lane the goal-line slant must occupy. Tell cue: Corners line up 9 yards deep directly over their receivers instead of pressed at the line — base 2-man never surrenders that much cushion.

## Coaching Lineage Trees (17 Trees / 53 Coaches)

### Shanahan / Kubiak Wide-Zone Tree (`shanahan-kubiak`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Bill Walsh → Mike Shanahan & Gary Kubiak (OFFENSE)
- **Description**: The most influential offensive lineage in modern NFL football. Stemming from Bill Walsh’s West Coast spacing and Mike Shanahan & Gary Kubiak’s legendary Denver Broncos zone-stretch run game. Powers today’s elite offenses led by Kyle Shanahan, Sean McVay, Klint Kubiak, Matt LaFleur, and Mike McDaniel through horizontal stretch runs, play-action deep shots, and disguise meshes identical for the first 1.2 seconds.

### Andy Reid West Coast / Spread RPO Tree (`reid-west-coast`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Bill Walsh → Andy Reid (OFFENSE)
- **Description**: A pillar of modern offensive innovation. Blends classic West Coast rhythm and pass spacing with modern college Spread RPOs, empty/bunch formations, Mesh shallow crosses, jet shovel screens, and 13-personnel tight-end power mismatches.

### Power Gap & Duo / QB Run-Game Tree (`power-gap-duo`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: John Harbaugh → Greg Roman (OFFENSE)
- **Description**: The downhill gap-scheme lineage: power, duo, counter, and pin-and-pull runs married to genuine quarterback run threat. Built on heavy personnel, play-action off identical run pictures, and forcing light boxes into unblockable run-pass conflicts.

### Pete Carroll / Robert Saleh Wide-9 & Match Tree (`carroll-saleh-wide9`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Pete Carroll → Robert Saleh (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: A defensive system defined by pure physical dominance and gap-integrity. Employs wide-9 defensive end splits and penetrating 3-techniques to create organic 4-man pressure, backed by disciplined Cover 3 Rip/Liz Match, split-field Cover 6 bracket coverages, and A-gap cross-dog fire zones.

### Mike Macdonald Sim-Pressure & Hybrid Disguise Tree (`macdonald-pressure`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: John Harbaugh → Mike Macdonald (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: The cutting edge of NFL defensive design. Built on pre-snap ambiguity, Double-A mug and Amoeba fronts, 4-man Simulated Pressures (Creepers) dropping interior linemen into throwing windows while sending DBs, post-snap split safety spins, and Cover 0 peel blitzes.

### Vic Fangio Two-High Shell & Quarters Tree (`fangio-two-high`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Vic Fangio (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: The defensive system that forced modern offenses to adapt. Shows a static two-high safety shell before the snap to disguise Cover 6, Cover 8, and Quarters match calls, paired with light 3-man Penny fronts to stifle explosive downfield crossers and force long, mistake-prone drives.

### Bill Belichick / Brian Flores Psycho Blitz Tree (`belichick-flores`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Bill Belichick → Brian Flores (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: A radical, highly aggressive defensive philosophy based on extreme binary pressure looks: either sending 6-7 rushers in all-out Cover 0 house blitzes, or bluffing everybody and dropping 8 into muddy coverage zones.

### Air Coryell / Run and Shoot Vertical Passing Tree (`coryell-vertical`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Don Coryell → June Jones (OFFENSE)
- **Description**: The ancestor of every modern vertical passing attack. Don Coryell’s one-back Air Coryell route tree forced defenses to defend the entire depth of the field for the first time; June Jones’ Run and Shoot made receivers into live read-routes who converted their patterns on the fly against coverage leverage.

### Air Raid Spacing Tree (`air-raid`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Hal Mumme → Mike Leach (OFFENSE)
- **Description**: The college game’s great equalizer: a handful of mesh, shallow, and stick spacing concepts repped thousands of times from empty and five-open formations, weaponizing distribution over play design and turning any coverage into a numbers problem.

### College Option & Spread Revolution Tree (`option-spread`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Paul Johnson / Urban Meyer / Chris Ault / Art Briles (OFFENSE)
- **Description**: Four parallel college revolutions that reshaped the run-pass interface: the flexbone triple option’s mathematical pitch geometry, Meyer’s spread-option zone read, Ault’s Pistol downhill physics, and Briles’ vertical choice shots off run action.

### Delaware Wing-T Deception Tree (`delaware-wing-t`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Tubby Raymond (OFFENSE)
- **Description**: Guard-pull buck sweep series with counter crisscross fakes and wingback motion — the gold standard of ball-handling deception, making three base plays look like nine through backfield choreography alone.

### Buddy Ryan 46 Pressure Tree (`buddy-46`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Buddy Ryan (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: The most radical base defense ever fielded: an eight-man box with zero deep-middle help, isolated press corners, and unblockable edge overload combinations that broke protection rules by arithmetic. Its DNA survives in every modern Bear front and mug pressure.

### LeBeau Zone Blitz Fire Zone Tree (`lebeau-zone-blitz`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Dick LeBeau → Dom Capers (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: The invention that changed defensive math forever: send five while dropping a lineman behind a fire zone, breaking slide-protection assignments without sacrificing zone integrity. The direct ancestor of today’s creeper and sim-pressure worlds.

### Landry Flex / Doomsday Front Tree (`landry-dallas`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Tom Landry → Jimmy Johnson (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: From the inventor of the 4-3 to its speed evolution: Landry’s staggered Flex alignments strangled sweeps with patient gap-zone convergence; Jimmy Johnson rebuilt Dallas with undersized penetration chaos that prefigured the modern attacking front.

### Phillips Two-Gap 3-4 Tree (`phillips-two-gap`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Bum Phillips (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: The revival of the modern 3-4: zero-tech nose two-gapping to free athletic linebackers, stand-up edge rushers as designated weapons, and second-level flow speed built specifically to counter Pittsburgh-style power football.

### Two-Deep Shell / Tampa 2 Tree (`two-deep-shell`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Tony Dungy → Lovie Smith / Marvin Lewis (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: Two safeties splitting the deep field as a committed identity: Tampa 2’s zone sink with the Mike running the deep hole, and Marvin Lewis’ red-zone 2-Man with pure man underneath — opposite underneath logic under an identical shell.

### Modern College Hybrid Front Tree (`college-defensive-fronts`)
- **Patriarch / Lineage**: Dave Aranda / Rocky Long (DEFENSE)
- **Description**: The current college counter-punch to spread offense: Aranda’s tite front (4i-0-4i) played from peso hybrid personnel to erase B-gaps against zone read, and Rocky Long’s 3-3-5 stack where every box defender is a potential blitzer behind total pre-snap ambiguity.

Philosophy: Undersized, hyper-fast linemen slanting upfield at the snap: pure penetration chaos, one-gap attacking fits, and coverage built to survive the resulti... Key Concepts: Zero-Tech Two-Gap Nose, Stand-Up Edge Duo, Over-the-Top LB Flow, Power Counter-Matches.

Key Concepts: 4i-0-4i Tite Box, Peso Hybrid Personnel, Apex Linebacker Splits, ILB-DL Simulated Exchanges.
- **Rocky Long** (`rocky-long`): 3-3-5 Stack Evangelist — San Diego State HC / New Mexico (1998-2019). Philosophy: Odd-stack defense where every box defender is a potential blitzer: constant slant-exchange games, safety/corner cross-dogs, and total pre-snap ambigui...
